body:
| | | Pundits will spend all week trying to name what’s happening tonight. We’ll save them the trouble:**** this isn’t just a wave, Peter. _It’s a tectonic shift._ **Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, and so far, dozens of our Working Families Slate champions are heading to the Congress.** Some of our biggest races are still too early to call, including the Senate race for **Abdul El-Sayed** in Michigan, but the night has already delivered a stinging rebuke of Trump and the Republican agenda, and the corporate politics that have failed working families for decades. Elon Musk and Donald Trump threw more than $800 million at this election to hold onto far-right control of Congress. **It wasn’t enough.** They had the money, the power, and the most powerful people in the U.S. on their side. We had volunteers knocking doors through winter snow and summer heat, and we outworked _every_ dollar they spent. Tonight, working people sent a new class of champions to Congress, and the billionaires couldn’t stop us. Come January, our champions will be fighting for lower costs, affordable healthcare, and an economy that works for all of us. **Let’s make sure they have a movement behind them.** [**Celebrate every Working Families Party champion headed to Congress by becoming a dues-paying WFP member with a recurring monthly donation of $10 or more.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30Q_DY_8HgrEUhTJQOSIJMi7Lk3JcpikEblJeqzx8jJZrDzlCqKghvyUmAn8EdUKXej2cX4GV_XvKYWusWRT94UUSC8yEq4nopPu1hPfG6A3M8L-isjeexwXTwAv9FofafgFJ_C2jv_4yPUKSwh_CGt3diuVHxzV28V6HjxcTxj-zQ192BuVxfuLbmrHf0zULGehr42mmEByOIyvvsJ6hNpAwEGLSn4MNSf37uI5hKniw45skmOK7lNMgoy55SIE-zg/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h0/h001.1t2vHAahdhGIMqjAcTBQQkaKaATNJXa_YW4yWrOy_VE) **[Become a WFP member »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30ZPY1CItPkUp-Mx3FAR4SUCf55GAvTkR1NB8O-KdbWleXGI_30FS_M4e94eIzMHjDfDQszYqk5FSKpBAznibkAV9NiNAbAlaKs8IATcAE8h23DS_Oz434sS0HQ6SWRv-hWE9eusv3NLblxxveW66tUo1QSnr0ZEww2paMYMzEUwF0EeohWagX5aXdM5W_gqglz0ob_Qc_agP15s3W5Gv_JCX6p8A_upj12NY49xxrtAR2N5-T64daWBSBh9Davz8fA/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h1/h001.xB_8mW676Twv4IOqwwRy-L1EeOynr_E_F8PKToqp0sU)** Results are still rolling in, and every update brings more good news. One of the biggest came out of Maine, where logger and union member **Troy Jackson** just defeated Republican Senator Susan Collins, ending her nearly 30-year run in the Senate and winning a seat Democrats haven’t held since 1988. And as House races are called across the country, some of the boldest WFP champions are making history:
* One of our first wins of the night came from one of our own: former New Jersey WFP state director **Analilia Mejia** (NJ-11). After winning an April special election for the House seat Mikie Sherrill left to become governor, she powered through a second hard-fought race and won a _full_ term in Congress tonight.
* In **Pennsylvania** , firefighter **Bob Brooks** (PA-07) just knocked off Republican Congressman Ryan Mackenzie, even with Trump pouring money into the race to save him. And in Philadelphia, **Chris Rabb** (PA-03), who took down the Democratic machine in his primary this spring, is officially headed to Congress.
* In **Ohio** , union ironworker **Brian Poindexter** (OH-07) is sending Max Miller, a former Trump aide and real estate heir, packing.
* **Michigan** isn’t finished, either. In Detroit, union organizer **Donavan McKinney** (MI-13), who toppled a multimillionaire incumbent in August, just sealed his win and is headed to Washington.
* In **Colorado** , **Melat Kiros** (CO-01), who made national headlines this year when she defeated a 30-year incumbent in her primary, is Denver’s next member of Congress.
* In **California** , teacher and longtime WFP member and leader **Randy Villegas** (CA-22) defeated David Valadao, who voted to gut Medicaid and to give ICE $38 million with no additional oversight.
* **New York** is sending a whole new class of fighters to Washington. Longtime WFP champion **Brad Lander** (NY-10), who was arrested by ICE last year while defending immigrant New Yorkers’ right to due process, is headed to Congress. Union organizer **Claire Valdez** (NY-07) will succeed Nydia Velazquez, while community organizer **Darializa Avila Chevalier** (NY-13), who unseated a five-term incumbent this summer, will represent Upper Manhattan.

These wins are just the beginning, and more races are still being counted across the country, including**Will Lawrence**(MI-07) in Michigan and four more WFP challengers in California:**Mai Vang**(CA-07),**Aisha Wahab**(CA-14),**Connie Chan**(CA-11), and**Angela Gonzales-Torres**(CA-34). [**For now, celebrate the biggest election night working people have had in years: become a dues-paying WFP member with a recurring monthly donation of $10 or more, and help us take this fight all the way to the White House in 2028.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30bY9ij5g0WBqPteYYVPkN62_wsD1i_Sq9j24LosRZQPHSQtVlj1IGMakjRZrEUeiRS8wFDNvqkqbVCXpxLZmO-xvjRASmlp4RQBz2gNFKoMfALZU10XzH7rCeKxew-uFuxozh5P_jnVkP9Er47WqODx-51NErQ3w6eTaYEutJSKT-DAdRL8Vvc_cO2oJgee0Yy6JgnQqofmUEDGjQMKvsQx7BTf1FfaSH8gAt6uOw3Fk5lGC2xMuCLItBgbcqOjFjg/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h2/h001.Lv3cBIIkWaFWm8rk6DH8B4EPK22MGBPrheBBROcbqt4) **[Become a WFP member](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30VS4kFL-M88vPhBYbWVZ9y5BEzMVjL8dYB9IOFy7vMAyM3PH4Y2FDN_QoT00mxi56-sqawq-8ImodQ8UTtYQKy82DCsH-uc0vMA8o1269XuCJFMp2JGR16qk_nb-uREX2R5a1Q5ojwzOd4OrNcHxb75L02kNvtDWm5QqUWdHAScWT5nNUhmunQZOP_Y3yaRa1gm67fKtAEnqT065A-1M0nfiNCbH1KriqXYNd7cm19ogYOiLF9tMovsjufUkdt5uhA/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h3/h001.tjbZbBsNGTmzGPeMtJDxHS1fKRa2rie0yEMvizIaxgk)** **This night was years in the making, Peter.** Trump promised to lower the cost of living. Instead he delivered _chaos_ , _war_ , and _rising costs_ , while his billionaire backers collected tax breaks and friendly regulators. Tonight, those broken promises came due, and voters sent Trump a clear message: you don’t get to _lie_ to working families and keep your majority. **He wasn’t the only one who got a message, though.** All cycle long, the corporate wing of the Democratic Party said candidates like ours couldn’t win. They said the only path to victory ran through _milquetoast_ moderates who promise _nothing_ and stand for even less. Then they spent millions in our primaries to make sure voters never got a real choice. It didn’t work. Voters chose every one of our priority congressional champions anyway. **And tonight, they did it again.** Trump and Musk poured more than $800 million into these midterms, much of it in the final months, and our candidates still won in exactly the places the corporate wing said they’d lose. So to every Democrat already eyeing a future run: **the path in 2028 runs through the Working Families Guarantee — a home you can afford, health care you can rely on, a good job to support your family, and childcare when and where you need it.** _That’s_ the agenda that won tonight. **And it won because of you, Peter.** Every one of the more than **30 million** calls, texts, and door knocks since January came from people who believed working families deserve better, and who gave their evenings, their weekends, and whatever they could spare to prove it. **That’s what our movement runs on. It’s what got us here tonight, and it’s what will carry us into 2027 and 2028.** [**Become a dues-paying WFP member with a recurring monthly donation of $10 or more to keep this movement growing, and make the Working Families Guarantee the agenda that wins in 2028.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30UYaoJg4ayDLRMNSdlI_WKFxO6zNyy8TZWuRkeZd2r_HaxYz1TxiKcTrahTsFFTL8RecrE_i7pUh8kI083tXJ6DcCih9Z0COhmf8qAjtb2RIRRC6Ulm3VDep3VfsRBZJaA6C6iAlpCjUWzLvEG5VAJjsWfOtWxD1KTaKiVtMGEOjGStCpU2KHJUpA_-OavUgxCA-5Z_nsZFSVw6tpxza4SP496VM-iqbfpdzreC3Ye0oZ0A2Nu0DUAilFhgJikNJAQ/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h4/h001.8OR3qpIjVfhvy9cub7unnW5gwyUZcmoAChF6iUPDR-o) Thank you for everything you did to make tonight possible, Peter. In solidarity, All of us at WFP P.S. We can’t let tonight end without celebrating **Angie Nixon** , who came just two points shy of a historic upset. After winning her primary despite being outraised nearly 16-to-1, Angie never wavered in her fight for working families, even as the Democratic establishment failed to rally behind her in the general election. clean_body: | | | Pundits will spend all week trying to name what’s happening tonight. We’ll save them the trouble:** this isn’t just a wave, Peter. It’s a tectonic shift. Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, and so far, dozens of our Working Families Slate champions are heading to the Congress. Some of our biggest races are still too early to call, including the Senate race for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, but the night has already delivered a stinging rebuke of Trump and the Republican agenda, and the corporate politics that have failed working families for decades. Elon Musk and Donald Trump threw more than $800 million at this election to hold onto far-right control of Congress. It wasn’t enough. They had the money, the power, and the most powerful people in the U.S. on their side. We had volunteers knocking doors through winter snow and summer heat, and we outworked every dollar they spent. Tonight, working people sent a new class of champions to Congress, and the billionaires couldn’t stop us. Come January, our champions will be fighting for lower costs, affordable healthcare, and an economy that works for all of us. Let’s make sure they have a movement behind them. Results are still rolling in, and every update brings more good news. One of the biggest came out of Maine, where logger and union member Troy Jackson just defeated Republican Senator Susan Collins, ending her nearly 30-year run in the Senate and winning a seat Democrats haven’t held since 1988. And as House races are called across the country, some of the boldest WFP champions are making history: One of our first wins of the night came from one of our own: former New Jersey WFP state director Analilia Mejia (NJ-11). After winning an April special election for the House seat Mikie Sherrill left to become governor, she powered through a second hard-fought race and won a full term in Congress tonight. In Pennsylvania , firefighter Bob Brooks (PA-07) just knocked off Republican Congressman Ryan Mackenzie, even with Trump pouring money into the race to save him. And in Philadelphia, Chris Rabb (PA-03), who took down the Democratic machine in his primary this spring, is officially headed to Congress. In Ohio , union ironworker Brian Poindexter (OH-07) is sending Max Miller, a former Trump aide and real estate heir, packing. Michigan isn’t finished, either. In Detroit, union organizer Donavan McKinney (MI-13), who toppled a multimillionaire incumbent in August, just sealed his win and is headed to Washington. In Colorado , Melat Kiros (CO-01), who made national headlines this year when she defeated a 30-year incumbent in her primary, is Denver’s next member of Congress. In California , teacher and longtime WFP member and leader Randy Villegas (CA-22) defeated David Valadao, who voted to gut Medicaid and to give ICE $38 million with no additional oversight. New York is sending a whole new class of fighters to Washington. Longtime WFP champion Brad Lander (NY-10), who was arrested by ICE last year while defending immigrant New Yorkers’ right to due process, is headed to Congress. Union organizer Claire Valdez (NY-07) will succeed Nydia Velazquez, while community organizer Darializa Avila Chevalier (NY-13), who unseated a five-term incumbent this summer, will represent Upper Manhattan. These wins are just the beginning, and more races are still being counted across the country, includingWill Lawrence(MI-07) in Michigan and four more WFP challengers in California:Mai Vang(CA-07),Aisha Wahab(CA-14),Connie Chan(CA-11), andAngela Gonzales-Torres(CA-34). This night was years in the making, Peter. Trump promised to lower the cost of living. Instead he delivered chaos , war , and rising costs , while his billionaire backers collected tax breaks and friendly regulators. Tonight, those broken promises came due, and voters sent Trump a clear message: you don’t get to lie to working families and keep your majority. He wasn’t the only one who got a message, though. All cycle long, the corporate wing of the Democratic Party said candidates like ours couldn’t win. They said the only path to victory ran through milquetoast moderates who promise nothing and stand for even less. Then they spent millions in our primaries to make sure voters never got a real choice. It didn’t work. Voters chose every one of our priority congressional champions anyway. And tonight, they did it again. Trump and Musk poured more than $800 million into these midterms, much of it in the final months, and our candidates still won in exactly the places the corporate wing said they’d lose. So to every Democrat already eyeing a future run: the path in 2028 runs through the Working Families Guarantee — a home you can afford, health care you can rely on, a good job to support your family, and childcare when and where you need it. That’s the agenda that won tonight. And it won because of you, Peter. Every one of the more than 30 million calls, texts, and door knocks since January came from people who believed working families deserve better, and who gave their evenings, their weekends, and whatever they could spare to prove it. That’s what our movement runs on. It’s what got us here tonight, and it’s what will carry us into 2027 and 2028. Thank you for everything you did to make tonight possible, Peter. In solidarity, All of us at WFP P.S. We can’t let tonight end without celebrating Angie Nixon , who came just two points shy of a historic upset. After winning her primary despite being outraised nearly 16-to-1, Angie never wavered in her fight for working families, even as the Democratic establishment failed to rally behind her in the general election. We’re so grateful for the heart and courage she poured into this campaign, and so proud to have stood beside her every step of the way. Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Do you remember the trucks?

I do. Refrigerated trailers backed up to the loading docks of hospitals in New York City, because the morgues inside were full. More than a year later, about 750 bodies were still being kept in freezer trucks on the Brooklyn waterfront.

Do you remember Hart Island? A drone filmed men in white suits lowering plain pine boxes into a long trench, one beside the other. Americans watched that on the evening news and understood that it was really happening here.

Do you remember the hospital wards? Rows of strangers on ventilators, sedated and alone, with a machine breathing for them. New York was so short of those machines that the Governor ordered the National Guard to go take them from other hospitals.

And do you remember what you felt when the number climbed again that night?

You were afraid for your mother. You were afraid for your spouse. You did the math on your own age and your own lungs, and you were afraid for yourself.

For more than a million American families, that fear turned out to be justified.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA-wu1Djg1WbeLZRikb1rbocRup3QuibNXwBndN2TO52dQV8edDjbhf614lMsRHvy0exqlQl7yjDgClvBL__qcRVwhFN8gdMY9H7j93sl
I am going to make the man responsible answer for it, under oath.

Maybe your family is one of them.

Maybe they would not let you into the room, and a nurse in a plastic gown held a phone up to the pillow so you could say goodbye through a screen. Maybe you said “I love you” into that phone and never found out whether it was heard. Then you buried that person in front of ten people, standing six feet apart in the open air, with no singing allowed.

That is the part I cannot forgive. Not the virus — we have always had disease. The cruelty was in the rules they built around it, and in the men who wrote those rules and then refused to explain themselves.

So let me tell you what the man at the center of all of it did on July 29 of this year, when the United States Senate finally put him under subpoena.

Anthony Fauci raised his right hand and took the Fifth Amendment. Not once, and not twice. He took it 111 times.

He would not answer for the gain-of-function research his agency paid for at the Wuhan lab in Communist China. He would not answer for the years of concealment, deception and fraud that followed. He would not answer for a catastrophe that killed over a million Americans and more than 15 million people worldwide.

And in all of those 111 refusals, he never once said their names.

Innocent men do not take the Fifth 111 times.

So let me say plainly what not one politician in Washington has the spine to say.

Anthony Fauci is a criminal.

His agency paid for the creation of a weapon in a Communist Chinese laboratory, and then he lied to your face about it for years. Over a million of our countrymen are dead. In my judgment that is not incompetence and it is not bad luck — it is MASS MURDER, and I intend to prove it in a court of law.

name: Jocelyn Benson
subject: This victory is for all of us.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Thank you.

I am honored and humbled to be the next governor of the great state of
Michigan.

This is a victory for all of us. Yesterday, Michigan citizens spoke and
made history — electing the first all-woman ticket in Michigan history,
and the first back-to-back Democratic governors in generations.

I didn’t get here alone. This movement was carried by so many people — by
my fantastic running mate, Winnie Brinks, by my predecessor Governor
Whitmer, by my family, by my campaign staff, by volunteers all across our
great state, and most importantly, by people like you.

This
victory belongs to all of us.

For 22 months, we've traveled this state, listening to people in their
homes, at small businesses, on the job, and around kitchen tables.

And yesterday, Michiganders made their voices heard: They want lower
costs, more money in their pockets, good-paying jobs in their
neighborhoods, and more opportunity for their families.

That’s exactly why I ran for governor — and it’s how I’ll serve you.

I know the challenges ahead are serious. I know there will be
disagreements, difficult decisions, and days when the work feels harder
than we imagined.

But I also know what Michiganders can accomplish when we come together for
a common purpose. Michigan is a state that builds things, and now it’s our
turn to build the next chapter.

Michigan, you gave us this responsibility. We will meet it with everything
we have.

Thank you!

Jocelyn Benson

body:
I could not have reached this moment without you

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=13740%2E400544%2EUhHvtp)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17895?refcode=jtk1718-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13740%2E400544%2EUhHvtp)
Friend, Last night, New Mexicans sent a message loud and clear: They chose a future rooted in opportunity, not extremism. They chose leadership that puts New Mexico first, brings people together, and focuses relentlessly on what matters most to our families and communities. They chose a governor who will always put New Mexicans — not a President, not a political party — first.
**_And last night, those choices made history.
_**
I’m a daughter of Pueblo women, a New Mexican, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. Now, I’m the 33rd Governor of New Mexico — and the first Native American woman elected Governor in our nation’s history.
I could not have reached this moment without you. Every door knocked, every conversation had, every phone call made, every person who chipped in, and every person who believed in this campaign helped make this victory possible.

**_We won this race because of you._**
This is bigger than one campaign or one election. It is a moment generations of Pueblo women, Native communities, and New Mexicans have helped make possible. And I carry that history with me as I step into this responsibility.

**It is the honor of my lifetime to lead our beautiful state.** I will never take for granted the trust New Mexicans have placed in me, and I will spend every day working to make sure that trust is well placed.
Our campaign may be over, but our work is just beginning. I cannot wait to get to work building a New Mexico that works for ALL New Mexicans.

Thank you for believing in me, believing in this vision, and helping us make history together.
Our brightest days are ahead.
Be Fierce,

Deb Haaland
Governor-Elect, New Mexico

## Blackburn Wins as Green Concedes
Republican Marsha Blackburn [won Tennessee's race for governor](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL8GOpBtbBMKF9fQ5dor0dreBCsLjuxNUP7-xP3CdU8aaTTzfq7LFRKl_f4NGzrm27LjUQmZsSxbioxlQ8LAKe8F64u4Yg2LEsp2UnZCLxA4vXHR0EbnlZxAhxadHKdhnIRRql1dGG4XqbywUxyMicabi_JBRWsRvDZTm9xZKKXQUoqLFr2R3odRWzTKismKRguMiXPpeUXGfcdaEW_0yW8sfchbS25lftZm-GrU3Kj5OI7-A2vOZ9qo-bzVqPmZKXEKJ0LhFAhP9ATh4V9l7xgeWDuEQp-OEGJXIGAnpBRyMFr3K2_UFhefRyJK1Y6NFvcNEv2N4H8afDv1GwAA__8Y6IYv), becoming the first woman elected to the office in state history after Democrat Jerri Green conceded just after 10:30 p.m. last night. At 74, Blackburn, who campaigned with an endorsement from President Trump, will also be the oldest person ever elected governor of Tennessee. The race was tighter than pre-election polls showed, with Blackburn leading Green about 46% to 43% late Tuesday and independent David Hatley drawing roughly 9%. Blackburn [declared victory](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOtDa2OancPE3dLn2SmTsJazO2JG9Ccrbn8grXPdJI43mm-_bcnMUKd2_3IGWeVsSnjUiM5bloMBYDozomXIqWJ-RK1a_SJCmE6IDtTjP9MJFuTbYVYrJKd-iFeM0jBNoKdvdbohymBSiMD5sQeI4hFGYQQ8KtN5cS_YqFAKUEPBPQa_FuvpRGdTSwGSgUYCBOJeed2RMCWtF3OI7v7D0Ph9ttDvzozbD_0bOjZzP8-zfbs_5Shs5X1qNnB85EpO_0BUmH_HCiqk7XKm769bo_M_6LKn7aGPoNiqVO1DagIbJ9DsfsS02PE6KkaoZGwX3w1H87OA_nviy8jcAAP__FxGHzA) onstage in Nashville before the AP or NBC News had called the race. She'll succeed term-limited Gov. Bill Lee in January.
## Escaped Killer Caught in Missouri

In August 2026 the national debt passed $40 trillion.1 It was not
voted on. There was no ceremony. Most Americans found out from a
headline, if they found out at all.

Somebody has to absorb it

A debt that size does not simply sit there. It gets serviced,
refinanced, and eventually dealt with — and there are only three
ways to deal with it: raise taxes, cut spending, or reduce the real
value of what is owed by letting the currency weaken. The first two
require Congress to do something unpopular on the record. The third
requires nobody to do anything at all.

That is why the figure matters to a retirement account rather than
just to a budget committee. Every dollar in your IRA is a claim
denominated in the same currency the debt is denominated in.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
If the obligation is managed down in real terms, that happens through
your savings, not around them.

The evidence is already behind us. It takes roughly $1.95 today to
buy what a dollar bought in 2000.2 Nothing was confiscated. The unit
was simply worth less each year, and savers holding it carried the
cost quietly.

Gold is the one asset in this conversation with no issuer. No
treasury can print it, no company can dilute it, no counterparty can
default on it. Central banks themselves have been buying more than a
thousand tons a year.3 They are not doing it for the yield.

You are allowed to hold physical gold inside an IRA. Most savers
have never been told that, because the firms holding their money do
not sell it. The free 2026 Gold IRA Guide walks through exactly how a
rollover from an IRA, 401(k) or TSP works, which metals the IRS
allows, how insured depository storage works, and the mistakes that
cost retirees the most. It is free and it takes about thirty seconds
to request.

body:
Your gift of just $28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound and shares the hope of the gospel with a mother considering abortion.

| | | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckc-K3DAMh5_GuWWw7PwZH3JYGnLqlnYp7TEospyYdZzgOLP07cuUGeh5j_okfSD9fr-Or-iDj_M3XLlL2Y3pGIkDTwkz54UnxjP_2Vzkj-BHJVVTApSyGpGyv_FYYWE7SxaBCu6gNbo1cFWyWDoHyjZVWxviGkxrr5pqZyVachUYB4Xv7j4AWQFoCfVlks7U0uG1bifJVS0qiYFTviTezyl4wpjxeHdbIr7QthahW3LeD6FfhBqEGmZ_83G-7ImnLcX7iFDDoxJqoIXpfTuzUANSSRg4WkzlKvRwCN1_efkKUjXf34RqCNcd_RyF7mttjAGhmjOv43_8uf_orGz9uQrd84o-POCxnYlY6H5P27EzZR_np2mLmWMWuv-lxh9t-fZzKJ__KFJn9w8fgj-aVlRyviv_XZw_GdKtU38DAAD__45vog4)
---
Dear Advocate for Life, Imagine a young woman who has just discovered she's pregnant. She's frightened, overwhelmed, and unsure of what to do next. Maybe she hasn't told anyone. Maybe someone in her life is pressuring her to have an abortion. But what if, before making that decision, she had the opportunity to see her baby for the very first time? **That's the life-changing opportunity your gift to PreBorn! can help provide.** Through our PreBorn! Network Clinics across America, mothers facing unexpected pregnancies receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear the gospel of Jesus Christ. ## Democrats Win House, Senate
Democrats [won control](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAUhE8DnSMeEBsXFNu4y7ZbWgQegSyYCN4myu1XyRX-bqQZfdJ8fy77xeWSj9tvV9FSbPuBr1GQCPsesA5yf9G349ZxjEdx7xZjd7sUcp4AJqF35yk_cQcebESUqDhaWFa1rGBWyZP1qxQzuDWeMSxL0Ffjw1n7II3T2s9Xnu0HByA0gAIlTt54BUZclQMzuxiZFhgytX66t3xQwlje7Yn95FvlxSaix2DqF5MbkxslTLmUT8fkllrFz6Nv_DeQyW0Go82ip4C1-e5oTL7kw6fpO5iqu7ee6c3kxrsNj1cuJY95YVrcqstfMKefqXpa-T8AAP__kpp-mw) of the U.S. House and Senate last night, flipping both chambers and setting up divided government for the final two years of President Trump's term. In the House, the party needed a net gain of just three seats. Projections put it far above the 218 needed for a majority, in what could be the party's [biggest House majority](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDkO2zAURE9DdRS4KFoKFmnUOW1K4Yv8tBhzEchvC759YBe5QOoZDN6837ftBiGGfP8FCQ35smW8WkQirJvD1AgeaEu-V2ztjPAu3lfYlFAjl5KLYQNL4YWb7JzxiAp1h0ZOi54WOS-qO4wGIQfY9YIel1mo3dnd4Q85wYIWYO-C-cxJKQYptdSit7PVcha7BjmP4D0bBLpApfZ_Ssh0oI_v8sLa25K6aA6iszH9k6mVqfW6rj7v9nPjkzO1niUGCrYxtX65MaKlUDJTq8NUbAVq_CjPhtyWTLVEnoIjrOlflV8hN071mU5uD7QPXm2GUWi9TF017rxCjKGNExvEPUGIXzT6P6Evo_4GAAD__9kijeM) in nearly two decades. The size of the [new Senate majority](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8GOkcMODYuKF7jLq_d0hqbIWYXTASjRPn7lXc_Yeuje6R7Pm7LDWOKx_0_ZnIcynLQqyViprp4yo3xi7Zy3Cu19kj4LiFUXLTSQwfQqX7BjeOTFpDeBSJNRpKDcTLjBHbScndmBat0GHrSI6CfCMkTgl5xhXUdg4zu1AGoHsCAUZfNbgasWg2CHTAE0SvykUu9fJZ48E4hvcuT6mUrWSa3Mz-aMP-EnoWeeac9pnQyoee9ZDofCT03OpBJ6HkAezX22nnKZavIrXvFo_vFXY6eqeZzIKvzj1dMKbZhFL26Z4w_Xsl_K_V0-jsAAP__ead-mA) was still awaiting final results at _The Flyover_ 's deadline. Democrats flipped Republican-held seats in North Carolina, South Carolina, Texas, and Ohio, among others. [Full results here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ_GdEEeG2EoXNyGLrfdEjlmnMyuf5A9AuXtV-QVtj1H-nTO93Vf744i5ed_l9ByKGvGs0VkxrpumBq7H_QlPyu2tkf3LiFUtyqpxhvATQ6r80wHrtBtNiAq1B1aMLM2M0yz6l4WdJhh1jPKSeHkR2VwG40LwRhnwMuO7IUDkAOABi17P3kNk3xoB9PoQhCDxI241P67UOYXhvguB9bel9RF-2Lem9D_hFqEWs7z7PPDXzeuXqhlL5GYfBNq-ezGiJ6p5CtItDHW1Lpqt_2kGKmNRgzymRzFD5__ZuWw6jcAAP__P6d3Ig). The majority hands Democrats committee gavels and subpoena power over the administration. Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress convenes Jan. 3.
## Upsets Topple GOP in Red Strongholds
Democrats took key victories in GOP strongholds last night, most prominently in Texas, where state Rep. James Talarico [defeated Ken Paxton](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u7CAQxfGnwZ1XDFgYFxS3cbe3TWnNwmCTYGPBZD_ePtq8Quoj_aTz_7guV0w5Het_3MlxLMtBj5aJmeoSaG-MX-TLsVZq7cz4KjFWXJRUpgfo5bCg53SnBbrgIpEi3ZGDcdLjBHZS3ea0n8wQbmQiBWlGC4PR0QdrLXp7G6BL7s0ByAFAg5YXb70GK28awRqMUQySQuJSL58lHbxRzK9yp3rxZe-y25jPJvQ_oWahZt5oSzm_N6Hmrez0fiTU7HE_Ma2HULOB0YBWPWPGmnzpA0VCbv2JTy5Hz_TEo_8-G7FQc1ddOB8p59TMKAa57ph-_Y7_Vuzu1E8AAAD___gigQQ) for Senate, becoming the first Democrat to win statewide there since 1994. Also on the Texas ballot, Gina Hinojosa [unseated Gov. Greg Abbott](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ugzAUhZ8GNiP_ECCDhy5s6doRXexr49TYkX0bmrevyCt0u9LV-XS-83VbbhBiSP4TdtTk8pLwqBGJsCwW90rwjSYnX7DWR4RXdq7AIrkcmBCM9wsYCk9cRGu1Q5SoWtRivKrxKqarbDd9gd5aFP0FFbcrB7NahSMfRgkKbY9t0CdOCN4LoYTinZmMEhNfFYhpAOeanqMNlEt3zyHRhi6-8hNLZ_LeRr0RPWqjPho5N3I-jqMzaz01zn8j5_Ns5Ez4C5X5M5hyYRjRUMiJvV18Qc9gXTMR8yEB20LK91yBFaw_kU5AW7R9HCHGUIex6bnfIcR3B_rfck8t_wIAAP__J6WFbQ), who was seeking a fourth term, and will be the state's first Latina governor. In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton, a Methodist megachurch pastor and first-time candidate, [unseated Sen. Roger Marshall](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO5CAQRb8GZ7Qo8PgREGzibDbd0KqBwmaHhwWlHvXfr9y_sPGVztU5fz73T4wpluM3ZrIc6l7opydiprZ7yp3xm1wtR6Per4SvGkLDXSs9SQCpxh0dxyftMHgbiDSZgSzMq5lXWFY9nNZ_gDdfjggBgkPC1a_aKK0MrsHQxxDtjQNQI4ABox5ucQYW9WUQlglDEKMiH7m2x98aC58U0qs-qT1czUOyJ_PVhfkl9Cb0xiedMaV7E3o7a6bbSOjNYb4wHkXobYJFzxNIT7m6hizRY5Yn5pi4FhlSvLr8xtKxy04FmWQnZPnWztEztXwjh2b99RNTin2axaiOjPH9PPD_tXxa_S8AAP__40eKTA), becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the state since 1932. In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown [reclaimed his Senate seat](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAQhU-DO1vMgPxTUKRxt2lTWhgPaxJsVjBZtLePvFdI96QnvZ_v67bcbIjhvH_agwz7tJxUSyRmystGR2H7Qy6d90ylPKJ9Je-zXVBi3wK0Ui_WcXjSAs1mPBGSasjAMKlhgnHCZjcAEgYa5aRpRO1B61Wp3rltWEEDYRPMFQcgNYACJTs3OgWjXJWFsbfeCy1pC5xy953CyTv5-EpPyp1LRxPNzvwoQn0InAXOtdbOreW6cfkC50sKnNMeUvseXui0TO3-W5i2ds2pngLnJpvtUUOMofSD0PJ-2BDfFfw_ME-DfwEAAP__-_V3PQ) from appointed GOP Sen. ## Ukraine Peace Negotiations Set
The United States will [mediate peace negotiations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OwyAQRk-DOyIYHP8UFNu4y7ZbWhMY7NlgsAxJlNuvkits_el7T3o_l_mCHDkt37iRrSHPiZ4lUq10zJ62UvFGLqfloFL2iK8cwoEzKOik1lK1M7rKD5p1420gAjINWd2Pph_1MEKzWn_2iMY7IBhaCEYRoBnPzoE-B_B9w_aN01q1Whtt1MkNzuhBXQ3qocMQRKvIc83H6TdzqiuF-MoPOk4ub020a617EeZLwCRgqiutHON7EzDtObJ7CZg4VToSVs4Jo4Cp06MaeyOfXG85BIkp5XtyVCRe79KveGW5EzqSiZZc-fMsAqbmsH5_coxcul60atmQP7am_q_fw8JfAAAA__-KBYab) between Ukraine and Russia next week on Nov. 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi, according to U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff. In preparation, American negotiators meet first [this week in Brussels](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unTAQhJ8GOiOvTfgpXKQ53U2bEi32GjYYjGxzyHn7iLzCbWek0Xzf76_pCznwsfzCnUzxcTrozoFKoTQ52nPBjWw8lkQ5nwE_0fuEk5KqEwBCthPawm-aoHbGEynSNRnoR92PMIyqXo32dpDoOnDt3CnXw9jNSsHo-x-dpRlrNs8cgGwBNGjZ2MFqGOSsEYYOva9aSY5LTM2fyEdZyYdPfFNqbNzrYNZSzlzpn5V6Vep133fj498H4-mfJKbgKvW6stjJMRYS12njzsciri0hHyTSlTOjKBi2LHC-hFtxZnFz2aL3IuMn18m48-YQOHd91cplRw7_L5TviXsb9S8AAP__sWqF0Q), Belgium, with France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the EU, and NATO to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine. Closer to home, First Lady Melania Trump [will host officials](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQhZ8GOpDH9vJTuLgN3d42JZrY42WyBiPbu4S3j8grpPukIx2d833c5zty4O3xH1cyxcd5oyMHKoXS7GjNBZ9k4_ZIlPMe8IzeJ5ylkF0D0Ag9oy38phlqZzyRJFWTgX5U_QjDKOvFaO-wI5Be907fQI1CAQ5CeCdw8Lar2Vx1AEIDKFCitYNVMIhPhTB06H2lBTkuMbVfkbeykA9nfFNqbVzrYJZS9lypf5WcKjkdx9GeuMR4pZWcrj-VnPYYuLC9EFNhG-jClQJujM0Sc2lez4S8UZNeOTM29F0SxuR4w3Q2oG-90rdOtEtZQ52M2w8OgXPXV1o8VuTwO6f8TeLbyJ8AAAD__wN8iDI) from both countries at the White House on Thursday, the White House said, calling it an “extraordinary moment in American history.” She brokered last month’s local ceasefire that moved hundreds of civilians out of Russian-occupied Oleshky. President Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping could also [meet about the war](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAQxfGnMZ2Rx-byUbi4Dd2mTYkGM16cNRjZw5J9-2jzCqmP9NPR__M23TDEsN8_cCPLPk07XSUSM-Vpoa0wPsil_Z6plCPiK3mfcdJKtxJAqmZCx-FJE1SL9USaTEUWusF0A_SDrlarjJuXHlw79157dEqDG7zX6h921JCvgn1zAKoBMGBU7XpnoFezQehb9F40ipbAKddfKey8ko-v9KRcu7RV0a7MRxHmv9Cj0ON1XbXbZ_cehR7ftNAjgNCjMkKP-SwloDwfGcNO8iB0JBnjo0icT7msOAfJ-dwOeZwcdvkd6pW3WGW7HFeIMZS2E426bxji7wP-W7en1T8BAAD__7MngqY) in the coming weeks. The Kremlin said yesterday that it hopes to finalize plans for a three-way meeting, which Moscow has proposed to hold at an economic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18-19.

**Good Morning!** **On this day in 1835** , delegates to the Texas Consultation finally [reached a quorum](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAUheGnwVssuGATBoYu3tK1I8LmEqMSiOA2Tt--Sl6h41l-6TtfF3fxKady_fQ3tPSM1RU8ekYibA4zbpRqadh_MvV6x-ZfOzjgMJ-EOHHl_EbpgU4Mwa48GDGgFdpIbeR8VsNuFeo4yyj5-RwnMH6DADGaWa5xDmpah2RfNSG4EsAFqFFqNQFoM-kJApeBKY4hUW0j7Uj49D3m3_rANm71NmS7E907kx8MFgbLcRwj9d3XklPBsbYrg2X3Jay1fjNYsFBL2BksWy0v15s0NBvuR8o59Vkzxa83n_K7T_-85WHhLwAA__-Lm3jZ) at San Felipe de Austin and chose Branch T. Archer to preside. Nine days later, they formed a provisional government and named Sam Houston army commander. Have you heard you're not supposed to drink coffee on an empty stomach? The warning is all over social media, and it claims that the first cup before breakfast is doing damage you can't feel. Gastroenterologists just weighed in, and their answer isn't what the internet says. Researchers performed endoscopies on more than 8,000 people to test the claim. A separate experiment found one common morning combo that backfires, sending blood sugar climbing when you'd least want it. So is your pre-breakfast cup safe or not? Ayla has the full story on today's episode of _The Flyover Podcast_. ## Hinojosa Makes History
Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa [defeated Gov. Greg Abbott](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO8yAQBeDT4M4WDGBCQfE37vK3W1rYTGwkAhbMxtnbr5wrbDka6Xt67-s-331MMW___RMdvR9lzni2hERYZ0y4Uiy5YvtO1MqB1V93mIHD2AvRczX7leILZ9EFt_BgRYdOGCuNleNNdbtbhLGj5SjXcXlIAK3DDUatuASjl5vvors0IbgSwAWoQRqlAYzVRkPgMjDFMUQqdaAdCd--PdJPeWEd1vLsktuJjsbkPwYTg-k8z2Hda8nXl8F09WEw-UpxTchg-gj9dgG51N4vSyHqt5h9D6CsUdYMx3501YXjjCnFNhqm-Pb0MX0S6Y9DvRz8BgAA__9vIXx7) on Tuesday, becoming Texas' first Latina governor and ending Republican control of the office that began in 1995. She led 57% to 42% when Abbott conceded. Abbott called Hinojosa to concede, then [told supporters](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O6yAQBeCnwR0RjPEPBcVt3OW2W1oYBhstMRFMnOTtV17tPsGWo5HO0Xc-rvPVxhT39b-9oaFXyPOOz5qQCMuMCR3FvBesj0Q137HY8_YzCOi5lFyo2TqKB86y8WYRXssGjRx0O-i2H1WzGb_0XdBLGP1oRetdF7SyoJ3SoxhDr5tozjQphZIgJKhLO6gOYNDd0IEXrWdKoI-Uy4U2JHzZGtI7H1guLt-aZDaie2XtPwYTg-kz5Bcd54vBdGIYTCk7mxhMaz74WnDldlkyEafMn5bcxn-l3Ns3_-HyuHP7qBT3phh_f8aUYu0HpsR6szF9l9MfNzsMfAUAAP__qm2DJA) in Austin, "_There are still votes to be counted, but mathematically, we're not going to be able to win this election_." He pledged to help her team with the transition. "_Everything is bigger in Texas, including the shock of this win_ ," Hinojosa [told a cheering crowd](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SnTAQhE8DmSj9IhQocEK2Th1SAg0wtkCUNPt4e3sXe4UNp6a6v-7-8zF9BEx4br_DAZ7ea55OuGsCIigTJFgI81mgfiaq-YISnjtOksueCcG4nsJC-IJJtNHPPDrRghfWKetUP-h294ObQSizSusGbRflpDHGrWsYoDdSqBb94yYE10JyIXWnrDZSWmeskZGr2GgOESmXjnYgeIe6pq_8gtIt-WiT34mu2qhfjRwbOd733a35_dR4_o0cr5yQcKmNHCMceSmB2IZnYDue-W-ugVX6PCsL85yJ2BH-QWU7Vsrli61YKrEU6BF8w9n2sM9c2uLjdWNKWHvbaL4dAdN3JvrhlC8v_wcAAP__tHGMRg) in Austin. The Rio Grande Valley native added that no one imagined "a little girl from the RGV would stand before you here as the next governor." "_It never bothered me that they doubted me, it bothered me that they doubted us_ ," Hinojosa [said in her speech](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAMhp8mbEGJCQSGDF3YrmtHlEvMETWXIOKD69tXnK5P0MmybH32_31dposNMaTbp72joeecp4RHiUiE24QRHYWcNiyPSCWvuNmz9xMI6LiUXKjJOgo7TrLy5ir8ICs0Ug-NHpquV9ViBtH3re362dtW69mr-doJDQ7sMLi-U1UwJ01KoSQICaputGoB9NDqFrxoPFMCfaC81bQg4dOWOf7kHbfa5XsVzUK0FtZ8MBgZjMdx1C4G9w1LfhTK6dxiMHp0oYSc-HmNwfguUjIYRcNgfJFfU_4XnKdwW4jHsCN_S-A2ef5YvSUsDMZqM349QoyhdJopcbvbEF9_0T917gZ-AwAA__8bpIhV). She is the first Democrat elected governor since Ann Richards in 1990.
## Talarico Flips U.S. Senate Seat
Democrat James Talarico [defeated Republican Ken Paxton](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL_GdI68xsC5cHENXa69Ejn2EiwtGNkbkvz9ifzClaMnjebN73W6-kRpu__4FR2_5jxt-KyEzFgmJAyc8lawPohr3rH4M8dJK91LAKnM5AOnAydoorupaKFBB4NtB9v2X6ZZHIDq0M69gh5UnGdlZ7RqgBZiZ2zomuTONgBlQCvQ5tIOptN6sN3Q6ajaKIzCmDiXCy_I-PJ1pnc-sFxCXhtyC_NeRfst9Cj0GG7VPyqn7aRCj6eP0CPl4Enocfcvzps8qmRPvqSQJS8oQ1535HSqyJAr01tW3DyjLD58MFbJWXoZKFdsiov7MxGl2g_CqPvqE33m8D9fPJz-CwAA__9iCIk5) on Tuesday, becoming the first Democrat Texans have elected to the U.S. Senate since 1988. With about two-thirds of the vote counted, he led roughly 59% to 39%. Paxton [conceded in a short speech](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO4yAQhJ8Gd0SwxnYoKK5xl2uvtPbMOkYCg2Dj5N7-5F_6n-AvRyPNzDd_HssDQwzH8zcmcvzZ8nLQu0ViprpQpJVDPiq1V-SWC1W8tF9AwSi1lsosuHI4adGdd3-Vt7ojpyfbT7Yf76bbnYHRqk2BIZy2O26WQOG4rdYOeCflu-CuNK2V0aA0mFs_mQFgssM0gFe9F0aRD5zrjXdi-mDb4r98Ur2tOXXR7cylif6XgFnAzDvtIcbLEzDvOdFFJGBeMRUMz0PAPGqrrNEyhpPkq3hkapLrKxWZgmeqSX6zN3mtEzBjKgLmrjpf3iHG0MZJGPVMGL66Ov7hfaeD_wEAAP__FaiEgA) Tuesday night. "_Well, let me start off by congratulating James Talarico_ ," he said, adding that he "_will be praying for him that he will do good for Texas and this nation_." Sen. John Cornyn, who lost the GOP nomination to Paxton in May, will hand his seat to Talarico on Jan. 3. "_The voters have spoken_ ," Cornyn [wrote on X](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwVsi7gWMPTBUlTxUSteOFoHrGImYCG6-3r5yX6HjOcNv-P-c5pNPOW2Xb38lx6-lzBs9WyZmqjNlCpzKVqndM7dyo-r3HWeU2B8ADlLPPnB60AxddGcZR-jIgR2VHVU_6G51i8IlhN72i_HQn89-kFGHAYMdYVDSdMntGoDUgBJQH5XVBtGOxhqMUkWhJcXEpR55JaaXb0t-lwfVYyjXLruV-daE-hA4CZxe-ytw-irr9lnq9t4ETo0935vACQHsgGpQYMAYqe2ouuri7ZlyTq23QsvL1af8R_M_izwc_gYAAP__J4ZyYg), offering to help with the transition. Talarico, a 37-year-old Austin state representative, will be the Senate's youngest member. He will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the Senate since Robert Krueger, who was [appointed in 1993](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnwZ0tWIixC4q_cZe_vdLawDpGIgbBXpx7-1PyCleORvpGmq_resWY4nH_jw9y_NryetDZEjFTXSmR55iPSu07ccuFKr5zWEHC2CvVS7Oi5_ikVXXB3WSYVUdO2VnbWY-T6XYXtDbjDQEUkbEbTX5Uk7kp3GiUI8guuremlDQKpAIzaGsuAHa-2AsEqYMwkkLkXAfeiemFbUs_-Ul18PnRJbczlyb0PwGLgOU8z8HvNR_vVsBScoocfROwYOXoEwlYGBPW6HNf8MX56D9q3-hApr6ipx7ATHaSeih76aoL5YwpxTZaYeT9gTF9xvmPnz0d_AYAAP__1maBcQ) to fill Lloyd Bentsen's vacancy.
## Democrats Lead Down-Ballot Races
Democrats also led all six of Texas' other statewide executive races on Tuesday, [according to returns](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0Luu4yAQBuCnwd1EMMbmuHCxjbuz7ZYWl3GCRCCCSZy8_Yqttj_dXKRP-v8_3_u3jSnm6297p5XfR9kznS0RM9WdEnmOJVdqz8StPKjavocdJc6gFEi9W8_xRbsawupkWNRAqzLLaJZx_tLDbQ1fYTLTjBqdm-RoSKOa3EzO0TLOzgxx7ZpSUiuUCvVlNHpCNMtkJgxyDEJLCpFLvfCNmN62HelTXlQvvtyHtN6YH02MvwRuArfzPC_Z-XCc_S1w64EEbo-SIkffx1QyQWNb4b9jh3MDLhDIx0BQMljIdIJlLjXTB66UqdoENgc4yrNC4RvVLjEBvck_exVQjiN6ah3I5QWjwE3LBZWcBW5DXcPjjCnFNhuh5fVuY_oXhH_Y_2vFvwEAAP__fBCciw) available at our deadline. Democratic state Rep. Vikki Goodwin led Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick 51.9% to 45.6%, as Patrick sought a fourth term. In the open race to succeed Ken Paxton as attorney general, Democratic state Sen. Nathan Johnson led Republican state Sen. Mayes Middleton 52% to 46%. For comptroller, Democratic state Sen. Sarah Eckhardt led acting Comptroller Don Huffines 51% to 46%. Democrat Benjamin Flores led incumbent Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham 51.5% to 47%. For agriculture commissioner, Democrat Clayton Tucker led Republican Nate Sheets 51.4% to 46.8%. Sheets had ousted longtime Commissioner Sid Miller in the March primary. In the Railroad Commission race, Democrat Jon Rosenthal led Republican Bo French 52.6% to 45.6%.

According to a menopause specialist, when estrogen drops after 50, the relative balance of [a hormone called DHT rises](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkEGK4zAURE8j72KkL9myFloMBBNmcJhFQzfZCNn6TgSKHazvOLl9475CL4tXVBX12bnOxxSn69nf0dJrnN2EW05IhIvDhAPFeVowr4ny_MDF7zo44FAfhDhw5fxA8YlOFMH2PBhRoBXaSG1k3ajiZuumUmCGsR-MFL4y3NfjKBvfDBCwN6GIdk8TgisBXIAqpVYVgDaVriBwGZjiGCLNS0k3JHz5PKb3_MSlHOZ7keyN6JGZ_MOgZdBu21aO6_U97ZRB-_H_X1f_PZ8YtF9dezl1x8tulO0aA5NHxbViUOe1F0we8e5jcvsWl8kTFosNjy2mFHOtmeLXnf_U0i_felr4DgAA__8vNnvy). And DHT is known for one thing: shrinking hair follicles. That's why so many women who never had hair trouble in their 30s and 40s suddenly see it later. It's also why thickening shampoos and biotin gummies often disappoint. [They don't address what's happening at the follicle](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkEGK4zAURE8j72KkL9myFloMBBNmcJhFQzfZCNn6TgSKHazvOLl9475CL4tXVBX12bnOxxSn69nf0dJrnN2EW05IhIvDhAPFeVowr4ny_MDF7zo44FAfhDhw5fxA8YlOFMH2PBhRoBXaSG1k3ajiZuumUmCGsR-MFL4y3NfjKBvfDBCwN6GIdk8TgisBXIAqpVYVgDaVriBwGZjiGCLNS0k3JHz5PKb3_MSlHOZ7keyN6JGZ_MOgZdBu21aO6_U97ZRB-_H_X1f_PZ8YtF9dezl1x8tulO0aA5NHxbViUOe1F0we8e5jcvsWl8kTFosNjy2mFHOtmeLXnf_U0i_felr4DgAA__8vNnvy). The good news? She says many of those follicles aren't gone, just dormant. Her approach skips the serums and foams entirely. It's two capsules a day, built around a mineral pairing many women over 50 run low on. clean_body: A morning newsletter focused entirely on news from the state of Texas. If it’s important news inside TX state lines, we cover it. | | | | | | Wednesday, November 4, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning! On this day in 1835 , delegates to the Texas Consultation finally at San Felipe de Austin and chose Branch T. Archer to preside. This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College

| | Dear Fellow American, How are you today? Here on campus, it’s not unusual to see students wandering back and forth outside a classroom, practicing before a big test. It reminds me of the story of someone else who wandered around, searching for something he lost... **The Headless Horseman.** According to the legend, this Hessian soldier was decapitated by a cannonball during the Revolutionary War. Gruesome, right? Well, each night, his ghost rides through Sleepy Hollow, searching for his missing head. It’s the unforgettable image at the heart of Washington Irving’s “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.” But Irving’s story isn’t just a ghost story we tell around Halloween. **It’s a tale about what happens when people lose touch with their past.** The past is old stories, myths, landmarks, and traditions that connect the people of Sleepy Hollow to those who came before them. Irving understood something we desperately need to remember today: **A people who forget the stories that made them will lose the inheritance those stories built.** As in the town of Sleepy Hollow, too many Americans today are losing touch with the past — reframing or abandoning the founding stories and myths that built America. But those stories are too important to surrender, especially because no inheritance passes itself on. Someone must preserve it. Someone must teach it. And someone must make sure the next generation understands why it matters. That’s why Hillsdale College continues to teach great American works like “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow _._ ” The story is featured in our new **American Folktales** , an online course taught by Hillsdale College Professor Kevin Slack, who teaches about American politics, history, and culture here on campus. Professor Slack brings greater context and insight to familiar stories—revealing what memorable characters like Ichabod Crane and the Headless Horseman can teach us about human nature, early America, and the stories that shaped it. **The full short study is available now,** but to help you get even more from the course, **we’ve created a special American Folktales Study Guide that is available as a FREE download here:** **[https://info.hillsdale.edu/american-folk-tales](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c2O1DAMB_CnSW-t8tVpe-hhxTCCwyyCOXCMguO0FvkoTbqIt0dFOy_AzbL_8k-yv9_N3VKgtLzaiDOVYlx2ZsVS0O6wUlp83kuOWM96NZLLSytEy7WxUOkNjbaNm3spRj82OIthUsM0qEk169z3UvfTJAC4l15bQIABRz15P-IAoqH53CcE10JxJWTnBNcj9B5-aHe5-IlpfmzOVuwoFXJYIOdty4EqQenyvjRhXmvdClMvTN6YvFHyuVsphOJswA7dweTNRtwJbGp9Dj_bagMWpm4Fl4ipfsgOmbpyJXVvOfcQcXHZIf5i8nLUaEo-djgj257LhlApLe-jiI6OyNQVo6Xw3gQbN0tLYur6hM0J_3NNqYf7sxzk8BnPqWKqTF0_ffn2-Hh_eTVfh_bz49E-j9Pss9t-UwhULgPTfDmxDnJs6v--7G2WfwMAAP__JuarBw)** Inside this special resource, you’ll find background on the stories, key themes and characters, discussion questions, and insights you may not have considered. And if you’d like to do even more, **please support Hillsdale with your tax-deductible gift to help keep courses like this—and the College’s nationwide educational outreach on behalf of liberty—FREE for all who wish to learn.** **When you give to this effort, you’ll also receive access to the course.** For now, please download your free guide and discover for yourself why readers have turned to classic American folktales like the “Legend of Sleepy Hollow” for generations. As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. **Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027.** **But the legal battle is already raging. **Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. **These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. **

Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her. But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own. I'm Mark Trammell, CEO of theCenter for American Liberty , a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won't touch. And I'm asking you to help us fight for Luka. As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027. But the legal battle is already raging. Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. ## Hobbs Re-elected; Dems Gain
Gov. Katie Hobbs defeated Republican U.S. Rep. Andy Biggs to [win a second term](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGu3CAQxvHT4I4VDNjEBUUady9tSgvD4CXBYMHkWbunjxzlBq8fze_T_-fH-uFSTmX_4Q605N5xLXj1jETYVszoKdXSsP_J1GOuNaSyU11BwMSl5EKvZ6v9RE-rHIJVk5-NHtBKMyszm1HB8LQubkGoaPQsndu0UEb7WY3fIozeQBBDsvdDKYWWSowKHlGNYoKotBAqjjAxLTAkqu1BT3QtvWtxMb_qJ7aHr8eQ7ZPo7Ex9Z7AwWK7rerh3dEfKr_uAwXILDBYpGSxCM1h-O0rIn3XbOg8Y0VHnroQX39K-d36lwjv6WgInbAf_r_L9Rktt3G-d37H42eov9NQZLEOz4bxSzqlPhmmxHy7lfwvpy3U_LfwNAAD__9VFkPo) on Tuesday, according to projections. Her running mate, former Mesa Mayor John Giles, an independent, will become Arizona's first lieutenant governor, a newly created post. Unofficial returns showed Democrats [leading](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD3uozAUxE8DnZG_MKRwsQ3df9stkWM_w5MMRvZLSHL6VaLNCbYcaTQzv_nzM_84TLgvv90GltwrzjucNQERlBkSeMK8F6i3RDWmnAPuC-VZcmmYEIzr-Si5HuBpFm2wyvjLoFuwYrio4TL0SrarDaPpoVdyGK5RjcKP2gt-VUaOTkujQov2HSgE10LxXskuqp4bGZXmXMVemkZzCEi5dLSCK_jKu4vpme9QOp-3NtmV6KiN-tXIqZHTeZ5dzA_BjzXDjo-3qZHTF6iR04fgq1mALfviCD3zbg8YHEFlbgUX2L86VskRnBiAFeehMnAlPVnE5Vagsrrmsy02HCemhNUMjebL5jB99tF_f3u38m8AAAD__7DtkjU) every statewide race, including treasurer, an office Arizona hasn't elected a Democrat to since 1964. | Flying together with our sponsor [](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkE2K4zAUhE8j72L0Z9laaDEQTJjBYRYD02Qj1PaTI1AsIz3HJKdv3Ffo9VdUFd__wQ4uxLDMV_cAg-7t7QJ7iYAI2UKEEUNaMpQtYvExpSksMybLKVcnxk5U2jWnssKIllWTEWrUrazAsFaLVreN4NXdaNlS30kqlVaKq057qZ3r6DTqkXV6rII5ChmjkgnaCF570VDFvZCUCt9wRSSFKWDKNd7B5fBOi_PxlZ6Q6zE9qmjuiGsh4hfhPeH9vu-13-bXclDC-39__wzq9_VCeP8x9LfLcL4dQdFvYSLiLGkrCVdl-2REnOHhQrTHG1vQIVTZTOseYgxFtUTS-eDfs_hjZU_DvwIAAP__yCF9uA) **The Hormone Behind Thinning Hair After 50 (It 's Not Just a Men's Problem)** If your part has been widening, your ponytail feels thinner, or more hair is collecting in the shower drain, you're not imagining it. According to a menopause specialist, when estrogen drops after 50, the relative balance of [a hormone called DHT rises](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkE2K4zAUhE8j72L0Z9laaDEQTJjBYRYD02Qj1PaTI1AsIz3HJKdv3Ffo9VdUFd__wQ4uxLDMV_cAg-7t7QJ7iYAI2UKEEUNaMpQtYvExpSksMybLKVcnxk5U2jWnssKIllWTEWrUrazAsFaLVreN4NXdaNlS30kqlVaKq057qZ3r6DTqkXV6rII5ChmjkgnaCF570VDFvZCUCt9wRSSFKWDKNd7B5fBOi_PxlZ6Q6zE9qmjuiGsh4hfhPeH9vu-13-bXclDC-39__wzq9_VCeP8x9LfLcL4dQdFvYSLiLGkrCVdl-2REnOHhQrTHG1vQIVTZTOseYgxFtUTS-eDfs_hjZU_DvwIAAP__yCF9uA). And DHT is known for one thing: shrinking hair follicles. That's why so many women who never had hair trouble in their 30s and 40s suddenly see it later. It's also why thickening shampoos and biotin gummies often disappoint. [They don't address what's happening at the follicle](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkE2K4zAUhE8j72L0Z9laaDEQTJjBYRYD02Qj1PaTI1AsIz3HJKdv3Ffo9VdUFd__wQ4uxLDMV_cAg-7t7QJ7iYAI2UKEEUNaMpQtYvExpSksMybLKVcnxk5U2jWnssKIllWTEWrUrazAsFaLVreN4NXdaNlS30kqlVaKq057qZ3r6DTqkXV6rII5ChmjkgnaCF570VDFvZCUCt9wRSSFKWDKNd7B5fBOi_PxlZ6Q6zE9qmjuiGsh4hfhPeH9vu-13-bXclDC-39__wzq9_VCeP8x9LfLcL4dQdFvYSLiLGkrCVdl-2REnOHhQrTHG1vQIVTZTOseYgxFtUTS-eDfs_hjZU_DvwIAAP__yCF9uA). The good news? She says many of those follicles aren't gone, just dormant. Her approach skips the serums and foams entirely. It's two capsules a day, built around a mineral pairing many women over 50 run low on. Thank you Wake County!
Last night, you elected me as your next District Attorney. I'm humbled by your support, and ready to get to work on January 1st.
I'm going to be focused on justice and accountability. That means keeping families safe, going after violent criminals, and standing up for victims. And it means everyone gets treated the same under the law, no matter who they are or who they know.
It was a huge night for Democrats, too. Roy Cooper is headed to the U.S. Senate. Democrats flipped the U.S. House and the Senate in a major way. When I was in Congress, I voted for Hakeem Jeffries 19 times for Speaker. I'm very glad my friend is about to get that gavel.
So many of you knocked doors, made calls and showed up to make this happen. You earned it. The American people sent a clear message that they're tired of corruption and they want elected officials who will solve real problems.
Now I'd love to be able to take a victory lap and just celebrate these amazing wins for a minute. But I need to be straight with you. There are immediate fights coming very soon, and they won't wait. One is about who gets to prosecute corruption in North Carolina. The other is about whether this office has the people it needs to keep you safe.
### **The corruption fight**
Because the state capital is in Wake County, the Wake DA's office handles public corruption cases involving state government. When state money gets misspent or someone in power breaks the law, this is the office that decides whether or not to investigate and prosecute those cases.
Political corruption was the issue I heard about most on the campaign trail. People are fed up, and they should be.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4e1e3c20-1b4d-42f1-8526-fb0911494820?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, [The News & Observer reports](https://substack.com/redirect/4e1e3c20-1b4d-42f1-8526-fb0911494820?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Republican lawmakers are considering returning to Raleigh in just a few days and using the post-election lame duck session to strip the Wake DA's office of that authority.
We've seen this before. In 2016, after Roy Cooper won the governor's race, legislators held a lame duck session, stripped the incoming governor's power to appoint university trustees, and made his cabinet picks subject to Senate confirmation. They also tried to cut his political appointees from 1,500 to 425 and tried to take away his control of the State Board of Elections. Courts struck down those last two.
In 2024, after Josh Stein won the governor's race, lawmakers did it again. They used a Helene relief bill to move State Board of Elections appointments from the incoming governor to the Republican state auditor.
And we know what happens when politicians take corruption cases away from the capital. Texas did it in 2015. The Texas legislature passed a law that took corruption cases against state lawmakers out of Austin and handed them to a DA in each lawmaker's home county. So a legislator accused of corruption now gets charged or not charged by a prosecutor who runs for office in the same county, often from the same party. That's generally letting politicians pick their own friendly prosecutor. According to a 2021 Texas Observer investigation cited by the N&O, corruption prosecutions dropped significantly afterward. That's not accountability.
Here's my view. Any law that changes who prosecutes politicians, written by politicians, should get a lot of scrutiny. If a nurse or a truck driver breaks the law, they answer for it. The same has to be true for the most powerful people in state government.
I don't care if you're a Democrat or a Republican. If you break the law in Wake County, you'll be held accountable.
### **The funding fight**
I'm inheriting the worst funded District Attorney's office in North Carolina.
Mecklenburg County has 95 prosecutors. Wake has just 45. That's less than 65% of what the courts' own workload formula says we need.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/11f4f7a2-1971-4211-a3ef-0d3f5eaa3874?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This year, it looked like help was coming. [The Senate budget included 10 new prosecutors for Wake](https://substack.com/redirect/c0693dec-0b69-4220-9282-e629b11e110e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). By the time the final budget passed, every one of them was gone. The budget funded 18 new prosecutors across the state. Wake got zero.
Here's what that means for public safety. The average caseload for a Wake County prosecutor is over 2,500 cases a year. That's more than double the average caseload in Mecklenburg and Durham where its an average of just over 1,000 cases a year. When there aren't enough prosecutors, victims have to wait years rather than months for justice, and repeat offenders stay out on the streets much longer. We're all less safe as a result.
### **What 's next**
I'll keep pushing the General Assembly and the Wake County Board of Commissioners to fund this office. If a Wake DA bill drops in the General Assembly during the lame duck session you'll hear about it here first.
But those fights don't change how excited I am to do this job. There are some truly amazing public servants in the DAs office, and I can't wait to work alongside them.
### **Save the date**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b06593f-bf9d-4c02-ae3f-edb3df4df3d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I'm getting sworn in on Tuesday, January 5th, at 1 p.m. at the Wake County Justice Center. It's a public ceremony and everyone's invited.
You got us here, and I'll never forget it. I'm going to work every day to build a District Attorney's office worthy of the trust you've placed in me.
Wiley

Cinde Warmington is running for Governor because she believes that everyone in New Hampshire deserves leaders who are going to help them and their families get ahead. If you’d like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-gP0Xd1LL-Lub7Gk22PHy9ShbPgxu4DFRkJPyKXJZ7SucX1CdKgpVQPvMXIjKiagYZNJ54LFIKIpOtkR29qnwmAZLX-_-ehVjRTq0El2tz5BqDkdPWgrWX8JbAX4BDIKxuB3r1S_V4XRo85W4-EUOmeRS5iXhmiFeFXRuKoCh8i6wF0cTnxZ2BlGWJbgqgnENlW5HozYWKIyTm_qH3Esna2CQB-1dPuQlATtrXItuQFSyrF5mEEDT_hCUa-fxTjfaxAwY9k-S-9OWfK1KWqJH8qz6snHKHGvXLr1_1BR_U8K0L0M-bCIFIq37KZtt5bYVLo7Tsu1l8YQiBP72jjBIPnSlMxMbDKG5Wo2zq3W7ciSPh0gV3FTNuHyMBzTACbfamUWRwMGG8tQmdhDukjZCK/4vg/bC5vnnQfS2y5GjtxBui6bw/h0/h001.fq4HppnlhPLrawhuPo_LmVc2G83kLswnTdmvscgBOgo)

Thank you.
From the very beginning, this campaign was about putting the needs of working families first and fighting for a future where they can actually get ahead. It’s the very same fight I brought to the Executive Council, where I fought for Granite Staters who have been left behind for far too long.
While this isn’t the outcome we were hoping for, I am so proud of the race we ran and the support we earned across the state. I was honored to lead our party at the top of the ticket, and I’m heartened that this was such a close race even though we were outspent by more than 6 to 1.
I’m proud that we fought for public education, housing, and health care, and that we stood up against the corruption and self-dealing that has made its way to Concord from Washington. Most of all, I’m proud that we fought for a more affordable New Hampshire without ever compromising our values.
And I’m pleased that the fight for those values will continue with strong majorities on the Executive Council and in the Senate and House.
I called Kelly Ayotte to congratulate her on her victory. I wish her the best in her second term, and I hope she will work collaboratively with the newly elected Democratic majorities, because we have real challenges ahead. It will take all of us, working together, to tackle them.
I want to thank my husband Bill, my mom, my two kids, my four beautiful grandkids, and my entire family for their love and support every step of the way. I want to recognize my campaign team for their hard work and late nights. And thank you to every single volunteer, donor, and supporter who gave this campaign their all and fought hard for a better tomorrow.
Even if you’re disappointed, please don’t ever stop fighting. This work remains unfinished, and we need you.
Thank you, New Hampshire.
Cinde Warmington

clean_body: | Cinde Warmington is running for Governor because she believes that everyone in New Hampshire deserves leaders who are going to help them and their families get ahead. If you’d like to unsubscribe, | Thank you. From the very beginning, this campaign was about putting the needs of working families first and fighting for a future where they can actually get ahead. It’s the very same fight I brought to the Executive Council, where I fought for Granite Staters who have been left behind for far too long. While this isn’t the outcome we were hoping for, I am so proud of the race we ran and the support we earned across the state. I was honored to lead our party at the top of the ticket, and I’m heartened that this was such a close race even though we were outspent by more than 6 to 1. I’m proud that we fought for public education, housing, and health care, and that we stood up against the corruption and self-dealing that has made its way to Concord from Washington. Most of all, I’m proud that we fought for a more affordable New Hampshire without ever compromising our values. And I’m pleased that the fight for those values will continue with strong majorities on the Executive Council and in the Senate and House. I called Kelly Ayotte to congratulate her on her victory. I wish her the best in her second term, and I hope she will work collaboratively with the newly elected Democratic majorities, because we have real challenges ahead. It will take all of us, working together, to tackle them. I want to thank my husband Bill, my mom, my two kids, my four beautiful grandkids, and my entire family for their love and support every step of the way. I want to recognize my campaign team for their hard work and late nights. And thank you to every single volunteer, donor, and supporter who gave this campaign their all and fought hard for a better tomorrow. Even if you’re disappointed, please don’t ever stop fighting. This work remains unfinished, and we need you. Thank you, New Hampshire. Cinde Warmington * Follow us on social! Hey, my fellow angry Democrats. This morning, we're waking up to a landslide.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b9edac83-7674-48ac-a158-786410b88c31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The polls were wrong, but they were wrong because they did not capture the sheer slaughter of Republicans across the country. Republicans held on to plenty of seats, but Democrats broke through in places that were supposed to be out of reach.
Democrats have won control of the House and Senate. With races still being counted, we're waiting to see just how large those majorities will become.
Yesterday, I wrote that this election would be a litmus test. Would character matter? Would broken promises matter? Would people cross party lines when they had finally had enough?
**This morning, we have an answer.**
* * *
## Ohio Showed Up
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4397e5c2-def4-4e79-8522-4680f8cfcfd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ohio Democrats flipped the 7th and 15th Congressional Districts, with a third flip projected 10th.
**Brian Poindexter defeated Max Miller.** Don Leonard defeated Mike Carey. Kristina Knickerbocker declared victory over Mike Turner, with the Associated Press call still outstanding in the early-morning reporting.
Three Republican-held districts, with two flips called by AP and another projected by Decision Desk HQ. Think about that.
**Marcy Kaptur** also held on to her seat, despite Republicans redrawing her district to make it even harder for her to win. They made the district more Republican, and she survived anyway.
Amy Acton won the governor's race. Sherrod Brown is heading back to the Senate. Democrats made gains down the ballot and into the Statehouse.
For everyone who has spent years being told that Ohio is hopeless, that these districts cannot be won, and that running in them is a waste of time, take a moment this morning.
Look at what happened. I definitely have more to say about this.
* * *
## The Local Races Count, Too
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fb8d328f-d097-4f01-abc0-a532c6e27486?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Rep Elect Megan Coy
The gains reached into our local races.
Megan Coy defeated Mike Dovilla, flipping Ohio House District 17. That is a Statehouse seat going from Republican to Democrat.
Courtney Scheff's defeated Michael Gallagher the last Republican on the Cuyahoga County Council.
These races deserve attention alongside the congressional and statewide victories. Candidates, organizers, volunteers, and local parties put in the work in districts where winning was never guaranteed.
Congratulations to everyone who ran one of those hard races. You gave voters a choice, built an organization, and made Republicans defend seats they expected to keep.
* * *
## This Was a Rejection of Trump
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8772c2b9-3626-4e26-9f7f-0397b02ff05a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My read is straightforward: This was a mandate against Trump and his administration's betrayal of the American people.
Lower costs were promised. No more forever wars were promised. Instead, people got higher fuel costs, another prolonged war, and an administration surrounded by corruption and the use of public office for personal gain.
Voters had the opportunity to respond. They did.
The rejection reached beyond one candidate or one state. Republicans lost seats in places where Trump had won comfortably just two years ago.
I'll be writing more about what drove these results, what the polling missed, and what Democrats need to do with the power voters have handed them. There is plenty to examine.
But this morning, congratulations come first.
* * *
## Congratulations, Brian
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49bd60af-72fa-4898-a714-0e6766c40067?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Finally, I want to say congratulations to Brian Poindexter for flipping Ohio's Seventh District and kicking Max Miller out of Congress.
Brian was the right person, with the right team, at the right time.
His hard work, organization, and coalition building delivered. He put together the campaign that could win this district, and he won it.
Having run against Max twice myself, I know what goes into taking on that race. I know the work, the fundraising, and the challenge of convincing people that a district like this is worth fighting for.
Brian and his team got it done. They deserve this moment.
To everyone who won, everyone who volunteered, everyone who knocked doors, made calls, donated, and voted: Congratulations.
What a morning.

clean_body: Democratic landslide. Republican seats flipping across Ohio and the country. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? We need to find other ANGRY DEMOCRATS. Please consider sharing and subscribing to fuel the ANGER for change. Democratic landslide. Republican seats flipping across Ohio and the country. | | | Nov 4 | | | | | | | | | | | | Hey, my fellow angry Democrats. This morning, we're waking up to a landslide. | | ---|---|--- The polls were wrong, but they were wrong because they did not capture the sheer slaughter of Republicans across the country. Republicans held on to plenty of seats, but Democrats broke through in places that were supposed to be out of reach. Democrats have won control of the House and Senate. With races still being counted, we're waiting to see just how large those majorities will become. Yesterday, I wrote that this election would be a litmus test. Would character matter? Would broken promises matter? Would people cross party lines when they had finally had enough? This morning, we have an answer. Ohio Showed Up | | ---|---|--- Ohio Democrats flipped the 7th and 15th Congressional Districts, with a third flip projected 10th. Brian Poindexter defeated Max Miller. Don Leonard defeated Mike Carey. Kristina Knickerbocker declared victory over Mike Turner, with the Associated Press call still outstanding in the early-morning reporting. Three Republican-held districts, with two flips called by AP and another projected by Decision Desk HQ. Think about that. Marcy Kaptur also held on to her seat, despite Republicans redrawing her district to make it even harder for her to win. They made the district more Republican, and she survived anyway. Amy Acton won the governor's race. Sherrod Brown is heading back to the Senate. Democrats made gains down the ballot and into the Statehouse. For everyone who has spent years being told that Ohio is hopeless, that these districts cannot be won, and that running in them is a waste of time, take a moment this morning. Look at what happened. I definitely have more to say about this. The Local Races Count, Too | | ---|---|--- Rep Elect Megan Coy The gains reached into our local races. Megan Coy defeated Mike Dovilla, flipping Ohio House District 17. That is a Statehouse seat going from Republican to Democrat. Courtney Scheff's defeated Michael Gallagher the last Republican on the Cuyahoga County Council. These races deserve attention alongside the congressional and statewide victories. Candidates, organizers, volunteers, and local parties put in the work in districts where winning was never guaranteed. Congratulations to everyone who ran one of those hard races. You gave voters a choice, built an organization, and made Republicans defend seats they expected to keep. This Was a Rejection of Trump | | ---|---|--- My read is straightforward: This was a mandate against Trump and his administration's betrayal of the American people. Lower costs were promised. No more forever wars were promised. Instead, people got higher fuel costs, another prolonged war, and an administration surrounded by corruption and the use of public office for personal gain. Voters had the opportunity to respond. They did. The rejection reached beyond one candidate or one state. Republicans lost seats in places where Trump had won comfortably just two years ago. I'll be writing more about what drove these results, what the polling missed, and what Democrats need to do with the power voters have handed them. There is plenty to examine. But this morning, congratulations come first. Congratulations, Brian | | ---|---|--- Finally, I want to say congratulations to Brian Poindexter for flipping Ohio's Seventh District and kicking Max Miller out of Congress. Brian was the right person, with the right team, at the right time. His hard work, organization, and coalition building delivered. He put together the campaign that could win this district, and he won it. Having run against Max twice myself, I know what goes into taking on that race. I know the work, the fundraising, and the challenge of convincing people that a district like this is worth fighting for. Brian and his team got it done. They deserve this moment. To everyone who won, everyone who volunteered, everyone who knocked doors, made calls, donated, and voted: Congratulations. What a morning. Stay Angry. Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by supporting Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: We did it
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3880%2E251025%2EzGATDi ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3880%2E251025%2EzGATDi ]Abdul for US Senate

We did it, Michigan.

My name is Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, and I am proud and honored to be
the Senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.

Up until this moment, you might have noticed that I always say
‘insha’Allah” or God Willing whenever the outcome of this race is
mentioned.

Today, we turn that insha’Allah into Alhamdulillah — praise be to God.

This is ALL yours. Michigan, I can’t wait to serve you with the same
big-heartedness, open-mindedness, grit, and earnestness you’ve shown me.

You welcomed me to your homes, your churches, your synagogues, your VFW,
and union halls. You shared your moments of frustration and sadness and
vulnerability with me.

You gave me grace and strength in my lowest moments, and the hope and
inspiration that powered my best.

I hope to bring it all with me to Washington in your service. Thank you
for your trust, your belief, and your kindness. I will take it all with me
to Washington — and I hope to bring back the kind of leadership that more
than earns it.

The last month has brought the stakes of this election into sharp relief.
Ours is a movement built over the past year and a half campaigning across
Michigan’s biggest cities and smallest towns. We spoke of a brighter,
bigger, more hopeful Michigan. Theirs? An astroturfed corporate-funded
advertising campaign to deceive and distract. They preached hate and fear.

Day by day, Trump’s insults became uglier and coarser. But I got to spend
those days with you — learning about your struggles, your hopes, and the
things that inspire you. A mom of two kids with a genetic lung disease in
East Jordan, fighting the system to make sure her kids don’t lose the meds
they rely on to stay alive. Her hope? That they don’t have to struggle
with health insurance like she has.

A grandma on the East Side fighting to make sure the violence that took
her son doesn’t take her grandson, too. Her hope? An America where boys
get to grow up.

I met Josh, the UAW autoworker fighting the corporate bosses who hadn’t
raised their wages in two decades — despite billions in profit. They won
that fight. His hope? An America where every single worker gets the right
to a union.

I met a small business owner fighting to make sure that another heart
attack doesn’t take food off the table for his 30 employees or their
families. His hope? That his workers don’t have to worry about how they’ll
feed their families.

I didn’t get into this to defend myself. No. I got into this because their
fights are my fight — and their hopes are all of ours.

We don’t do this work for ourselves. We do this work for each other. To
defend us all from another generation’s youth, treasure, and opportunity
squandered at the altar of endless war. To defend us all from corporate
oligarchs who’ve bought and sold our government to rig the system against
us. To defend us all from a healthcare system more interested in
monetizing our illness than healing our bodies and minds. To defend us all
from air too putrid to breathe and water too putrid to drink. To defend us
all from losing our voting or reproductive or human rights.

I ran to defend us all from politicians who want to divide us rather than
movements that work to dignify us. Across our primary and general election
campaigns, they spent over 350 million dollars trying to beat us. That’s a
record here in Michigan. 70 million alone in the primary, funded by all
the same cats who funded the general election — that’s a record anywhere
in this country!

But we built something bigger than a bank account. We built a movement.
Government of the people, by the people, and for the people.

We showed that in a battle between the money and the many — that the many
can win.

Mike, enjoy your retirement in Florida. You chose hate. Michigan chose
hope. May we never have to see the likes of you in our state again.

JD, there’s a delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally
obligated to swear me in in January. Wolverine 1 - Buckeye 0.

Donald, I know you’ve struggled with my name. After JD swears me in in
January, you can just call me “Senator.”

To the Super PACs and special interests that tried to beat us, we’re
coming for your system of politics. To AIPAC, who spent $42 million
dollars against us, thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you
twice. They try to call you hateful if you believe that Palestinian kids
should get to grow up in the land of their forefathers without being
murdered by our tax dollars. If you believe in equal rights to peace,
dignity, and self-determination. That’s not hate. It’s love.

We showed that a movement of the people, by the people, and for the people
will ultimately win — Michigan understands solidarity. It’s the people who
decide who we send to Washington and what Washington will do. We decide —
not the big money or their stooges. The people of Michigan will be heard.

We showed that we can defeat a record 70 million dollars of outside
spending and an 11-1 money disadvantage in a primary election. That we can
defeat a quarter of a billion dollars in a general election. We can defeat
the cynicism of a politics that preys on our earnestness, undersells our
intelligence, and exploits our disagreements.

Michigan, we beat a machine. And we proved once again how big America
really is. Because where else but in America can a doctor named
Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, a child of immigrants raised by his father
and his daughter of the American revolution stepmother, get elected
senator from America’s greatest state?

To all of us: this fight is not yet over. The day I jumped into this race,
I promised you that I’d put in the work, fight the fights on your behalf.
I asked for your time, your energy, your support over the last 19 months.
Now, I’m asking for the next 6 years.

This work is bigger than one senator; it’s about changing our politics. So
please, don’t send me to DC all by myself. Come with me. Winning a single
US Senate seat was never the goal. The goal is to use that seat to
transform our politics.

The beauty and soul of America is that we, the people, are what America is
all about. We deserve an America for all of her kids.

Thank you,

Abdul

[1]Abdul El-Sayed

# Mansharamani Musings
---
| | [](https://us.list-manage.com/ul3rFEv94so?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)October had lots of developments that demanded attention. Producer prices rose faster than consumer prices, France ignited, and the bond market rioted. The AI boom attracted a lot of doubters, with rapidly spreading concerns that the bubble was bursting. And, surprise surprise, the American midterm elections increasingly dominated the news. See below for links to my thoughts about these (and other) topics as well as a midterm preview from a friend and DC insider...
Best wishes for a thought-filled November! _**
- Vikram**_

| | **OCTOBER 4, 2026**

Interest rates are on an upward march. The 10-year Treasury just hit 5.33%; the 30-year hit 5.69%. Those are 24-year highs. But this is not just an American phenomenon. The UK 30-year punched through 6% for the first time since 1998. France’s 10-year hit its highest since 2002. The bond market is telegraphing distress.

What is going on? The answer comes down to three forces. And they’re all connected.
**1\. Inflation: Stimulus & War**The inflation story started with COVID. Governments flooded their economies with trillions in stimulus, central banks monetized it, and demand came roaring back before supply chains could. That was the first wave. The second wave came from two wars. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine rapidly and massively disrupted the energy and grain markets, beginning in 2022 but continuing to the present. The Iran war compounded an already problematic situation: Goldman Sachs called the Iran War the largest oil...
