| | **OCTOBER 11, 2026**
The frozen pizza business is booming...and that’s concerning. That probably sounds strange. But not if you understand what frozen pizza actually _is,_ economically speaking. Frozen pizza isn’t a product. It’s a _signal_. And right now, the signal is flashing red.
You see, frozen pizza thrives when the economy doesn’t. In 2009, at the depths of the Great Recession, frozen pizza sales surged while restaurants sat empty. When COVID hit in 2020, [sales jumped roughly a billion dollars in a single year](https://us.list-manage.com/8sV_Rwivw56?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), from $5.6 billion to $6.6 billion. The pattern is proving so reliable, it’s almost mechanical: when families start trading down from dining out to eating in, that journey includes regular stops in the frozen food aisle.
And right now? The frozen aisle is as busy as ever.

| | **OCTOBER 18, 2026**

In March, [QatarEnergy declared _force majeure_](https://us.list-manage.com/ls29ctAlwNA?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) on its natural gas exports. One announcement, one simple sentence. And just like that, twenty percent of the world’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply went offline. Seven months later, it’s still dark. [In the first six months of the war](https://us.list-manage.com/LnSMBTxXO5H?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), Qatar shipped 18 LNG cargoes. In the same period the year before, it shipped 509. The lost sales are valued at around $24 billion. As of this writing, there’s still no firm date for resumption.
Natural gas supplies [about a quarter of the world’s energy](https://us.list-manage.com/j6gooJvl_gV?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), and LNG (gas chilled to negative 162 degrees Celsius until it liquefies and shrinks to one six-hundredth of its volume) is how it crosses oceans to countries that need it most. If you’re unfamiliar with how this actually happens...

| | **OCTOBER 25, 2026**

In 1972, a journalist asked Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai about the impact of the French Revolution. His answer, the story goes, was, “It’s too early to say.” The line has become a staple of geopolitical commentary. It’s a great reminder that revolutions unfold on very long timelines (and that the Chinese generally think about dynamics over the long-term compared vs. the short attention spans of the West). Interestingly, some thought Enlai was being asked about the then-more-recent 1968 student protests that had rocked the country, but whether he was referring to 1789 or 1968, the quote is worth keeping in mind, because, as this weekend’s activity showed, the next revolution seems to be underway.
It started with a high school in Créteil. On September 21, the day after their teachers went on strike, students at the Lycée Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry in the Paris suburbs walked out over unfilled teaching posts, classroom sizes of 35, and rooms without enough tables. By the end of the month, more than a thousand lycées were disrupted. On one day in particular, French police had arrested nearly 2,000 people (mostly minors). Within a month, the unrest had grown from just students to include teachers, parents, unions, farmers and Yellow Vest veterans. Hundreds of thousands of people were in the streets and the historic town hall in Limoges, a building that survived two world wars, was burning...

# NAVIGATING UNCERTAINTY
---
| | As many of you are aware, I’ve returned to writing my weekly newsletter and have been pleased by the rapidly growing interest in my thoughts. As I have in the past, I’m addressing a wide range of topics, ranging from geopolitics and economics to social trends to technology. The overall theme of my work is focused on “navigating uncertainty” and how a generalist approach can help us all make sense of what seems like chaos.

James O'Keefe spent nine years in court over one hidden camera. Here
is how it ended.

James O'Keefe spent nine years in court over one hidden camera. Here
is how it ended.

Dear Patriot,

My name is James O'Keefe. For twenty years I have sent undercover
reporters into places powerful people would rather you never see, and
I have published exactly what those cameras recorded.

THAT WORK MAKES ENEMIES, AND A NUMBER OF THEM RESPOND BY FILING
LAWSUITS.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
[Donation Page]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5

In 2016 we placed a reporter inside Democracy Partners, a Democratic
consulting firm founded by longtime operative Robert Creamer, whose
organizations worked with the Democratic National Committee during
that election. She accepted an unpaid role, answered phones, and
recorded what people around her said. We published it.

They sued me in June 2017, and a jury eventually found against us,
entering a $130,000 judgment on the books.

We appealed, and then we waited for years while continuing to pay
attorneys.

► WATCH JAMES O'KEEFE'S REACTION AND CHIP IN $35 ◄
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
On AUGUST 21, 2026, the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in our
favor TWO TO ONE, and the entire judgment was erased.

Here is why that decision matters far beyond me.

The verdict had rested on the idea that our undercover reporter owed a
FIDUCIARY DUTY to the organization she was investigating. Read that
again, because it would mean a journalist who takes an internship to
document wrongdoing is legally required to protect the interests of
the people committing it. That theory WOULD EFFECTIVELY END UNDERCOVER
REPORTING IN THIS COUNTRY.

The appeals court threw it out, holding that she was NEVER A FIDUCIARY
because she performed clerical tasks and had no power to act for the
firm. With the fiduciary theory gone, the wiretapping claims fell with
it. The judges also held that a plaintiff cannot collect damages when
protected speech, rather than unlawful conduct, caused the harm, and
they found that the "VAST SHARE" of our published material had been
lawfully obtained.

Nine years of my life, and the result is federal appellate case law
that protects the next reporter who does what we did.

► STAND WITH JAMES O'KEEFE. DONATE TO THE O'KEEFE DEFENSE FUND
HOSTED BY LIBERTY GUARD. ◄
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
I want you to understand the game being played here, because winning
was never really the objective.

People who cannot beat our reporting take us to court to drain us
instead. Depositions replace investigations, filing deadlines replace
field work, and legal invoices arrive every single month for nine
years running. If they can keep me busy and broke, they never have to
answer a single question our cameras raised.

That is why the O'KEEFE DEFENSE FUND exists. It pays the attorneys, it
keeps my reporters working, and it converts each attack into precedent
that protects the journalist who comes after us.

► CHIP IN $35 AND HELP US FIGHT THE NEXT ONE ◄
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
The fund is NEARLY EMPTY after this appeal, and other cases are still
open.

If you believe a reporter with a camera should be able to walk into a
room and show you the truth, then I am asking you to send whatever you
can today. Any amount helps, and all of it goes to the fight.

THEY HAD NINE YEARS TO BREAK ME. I AM UNDEFEATED.

For Liberty,[James O'Keefe]
James O'Keefe
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

P.S. The court's ruling did not simply clear a debt, it established a
rule that every undercover journalist in America can now stand on.

| | Yesterday, Democrats won big, electing new generations of leadership across the country. **Thank you all for giving us this experience of waking up today with hope. You took democracy into your own hands and stepped up to speak out against Trump's lawlessness and corruption.** And the voters were clear about why. 90% of voters say government corruption was a factor in their congressional vote. Voters stepped up for a new vision of politics where public servants work for the people to secure the future their families deserve. This is about building a future where every child, every senior, and every family can get the healthcare they need. Where our tax dollars go towards healthcare and housing, not wars and corruption. And where the American people can trust that Washington is working for them, not the billionaires or special interests. **I've always said election day is the starting line, not the finish line. body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=17%2E6803%2EOgbz03)
What a night.
**YOU, yes you, helped flip the flippin’ U.S. House and Senate! We’re changing who our government serves because of your support._Just take a look for yourself:_**
✅**In my home state of California, Randy Villegas unseated David Valadao!** He overcame over $14 million in spending against him to flip this seat. Randy ran on a fierce, unapologetic platform for working families, and he’s ready to take on polluters and the Washington establishment in D.C.
✅ **In Michigan, tens of millions in outside spending couldn’t stop Will Lawrence from flipping the 7th Congressional District. It was a close one,** but Will never compromised on his call for a national moratorium on runaway data centers. His victory proved that voters will not let AI tech monopolies treat our communities like their personal playground.
✅ **In Texas, Gina Hinojosa unseated one of the most powerful incumbents in the heart of oil and gas country!** She faced at least $281 million in spending from Greg Abbott _and_ millions from Elon Musk. But money couldn't stop her from making history as Texas's first Democratic governor in over three decades!
✅ **In Minnesota, Peggy Flanagan overcame millions in outside spending in the primary and a MAGA opponent in the general election.** She’s now the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate! JanePAC backed Peggy from the start, and we can’t wait to see fierce spirit in Washington.
A new day is here. I can feel it in my bones.
A few years ago, who could have imagined we'd elect climate champions in places where Big Oil once seemed untouchable?
Together, we’re restoring hope in what politics can be. Government _can_ work for the many, not just the privileged few. Every one of these climate champions is proof of that.
**I cannot tell you how honored I am to be part of this movement with you.**
Wherever you call home, these victories are _your_ victories. Volunteers knocked on doors, organizers brought communities together, and grassroots donors gave whatever they could.
THIS is what I’ve spent my life fighting for. The belief that every single one of us has the power to change things. That hope isn't sitting back and waiting for a better world to come along.
Hope is putting our values into action.
And last night, we did what we do best: **we showed up in numbers they couldn’t ignore.**
The many proved more powerful than the money. This new dawn belongs to all of us.
From the bottom of my heart, thank you.
xx Jane

name: Molly Gray
subject: We won. Thank you.
body:
I am still taking it all in. And before anything else, I wanted to say thank you. Dear Peter, Good morning! I am still taking it all in. And before anything else, **I wanted to say thank you. ** To the people who believed in this campaign from the very beginning, taking a chance on me wasn't necessarily the easiest decision: thank you. To our small but mighty campaign team, our interns, and the countless volunteers who knocked doors, made more than 50,000 calls, and sent over 125,000 text messages, _this victory belongs to you, too._ Over the last ten months, we traveled across Vermont, listened to our neighbors, and brought people into a conversation about a different future for our state. More than 1,600 Vermonters from all 14 counties helped fund this campaign. We did it without accepting a dime of corporate or corporate PAC money. And we won by focusing on the issues that matter: making health care more accessible, addressing our housing crisis, lowering costs for working families, and standing up for our neighbors and our shared values. We did it the Vermont way: by keeping it positive and focusing on solutions. We also showed that politics in Vermont can look different. That we can lift people up rather than tear them down. That we can bring people together across communities, backgrounds, and beliefs. And that we don't have to accept the status quo simply because that’s the way things have always been done. While I didn’t agree with his style of campaigning, I want to recognize John Rodgers and thank him for his 18 years of service and his advocacy for rural Vermont. I also want to thank Ryan McLaren and Esther Charlestin for their hard-fought campaigns in the primary, and every candidate across Vermont who stepped forward to serve their communities. There were some incredible wins in the legislature last evening. That being said, this election was not a mandate. It was an opportunity. An opportunity to urgently deliver meaningful results for Vermonters. I don’t take the support or the vote of a single Vermonter for granted. I know both the joy and optimism of a victory, and the very public pain of a loss. But here’s what I have learned: When you love Vermont, when you love her people, and when you believe in what her future can be, **there is no giving up. ** **Not when the outcome isn't what you hoped for. Not when times are difficult. Not ever. ** I understand the responsibility that comes with this office, and I promise to bring urgency, experience, and a willingness to work with anyone. I will fight for working families. I will work alongside our Legislature and statewide elected leaders to advance practical solutions that make life more affordable. And when Vermont’s rights and freedoms are threatened, I will stand shoulder to shoulder with our leaders to protect every Vermonter. From the very beginning, we said we weren’t just building a coalition to win an election. We were building a coalition to do some important work. Yesterday, we proved what is possible. Today, we get some rest and prepare for the work ahead. Thank you for believing in me and this campaign! clean_body: I am still taking it all in. And before anything else, I wanted to say thank you. Dear Peter, Good morning! I am still taking it all in. And before anything else, I wanted to say thank you. To the people who believed in this campaign from the very beginning, taking a chance on me wasn't necessarily the easiest decision: thank you. To our small but mighty campaign team, our interns, and the countless volunteers who knocked doors, made more than 50,000 calls, and sent over 125,000 text messages, this victory belongs to you, too. Over the last ten months, we traveled across Vermont, listened to our neighbors, and brought people into a conversation about a different future for our state. More than 1,600 Vermonters from all 14 counties helped fund this campaign. We did it without accepting a dime of corporate or corporate PAC money. And we won by focusing on the issues that matter: making health care more accessible, addressing our housing crisis, lowering costs for working families, and standing up for our neighbors and our shared values. We did it the Vermont way: by keeping it positive and focusing on solutions. We also showed that politics in Vermont can look different. That we can lift people up rather than tear them down. That we can bring people together across communities, backgrounds, and beliefs. And that we don't have to accept the status quo simply because that’s the way things have always been done. While I didn’t agree with his style of campaigning, I want to recognize John Rodgers and thank him for his 18 years of service and his advocacy for rural Vermont. I also want to thank Ryan McLaren and Esther Charlestin for their hard-fought campaigns in the primary, and every candidate across Vermont who stepped forward to serve their communities. There were some incredible wins in the legislature last evening. That being said, this election was not a mandate. It was an opportunity. An opportunity to urgently deliver meaningful results for Vermonters. I don’t take the support or the vote of a single Vermonter for granted. I know both the joy and optimism of a victory, and the very public pain of a loss. But here’s what I have learned: When you love Vermont, when you love her people, and when you believe in what her future can be, there is no giving up. Not when the outcome isn't what you hoped for. Not when times are difficult. Not ever. I understand the responsibility that comes with this office, and I promise to bring urgency, experience, and a willingness to work with anyone. I will fight for working families. I will work alongside our Legislature and statewide elected leaders to advance practical solutions that make life more affordable. And when Vermont’s rights and freedoms are threatened, I will stand shoulder to shoulder with our leaders to protect every Vermonter. From the very beginning, we said we weren’t just building a coalition to win an election. We were building a coalition to do some important work. Yesterday, we proved what is possible. Today, we get some rest and prepare for the work ahead. Thank you for believing in me and this campaign! | | | Peter, What a night. We’ve only got good news, because there is so much of it. **Here in Massachusetts,** we re-elected our incredible Constitutional officers, sending Governor Maura Healey and Lieutenant Governor Kim Driscoll back to the corner office to keep moving Massachusetts forward for every person in our great Commonwealth. In the State Legislature, we expanded our blue majority, and our fantastic Senator, Ed Markey, is heading back to the U.S. Senate to continue fighting for working-class people across Massachusetts and our nation. **And across the country,** Democrats have won back the House _and_ the Senate. We flipped governorships in Texas, Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, and Nevada, victories in states that so many had long written off. Voters rejected division and hate and instead chose leaders who will fight for them. But the scoreboard is only the beginning of the story. Here is what last night really means. It means people showed up. They looked at the cost of living, at their health care, at who is actually looking out for them, and they turned out in force to ask for something better. It means no place is out of reach. A Democrat is headed to the Senate from Texas for the first time in decades. Georgia has elected the first Black woman governor in American history. Maine sent Republican Senator Susan Collins packing, 100 days after engaging in an unprecedented process to nominate Troy Jackson. Democrats won races in states that even the most tuned-in of national pundits never bothered to get briefed on. So the next time someone tells you the map is set in stone, remember last night and smile. It means our values are not fragile. Right here in Massachusetts, voters upheld our gun safety law, passed Election Day registration, said no to big money in our primary elections, gave public defenders the right to unionize, and said no to repealing legal cannabis. That is our Commonwealth, speaking loudly and proudly. And it means that no race, in any state, is untouchable. So when someone tells you the best days are behind us, remember who you are and where you live. Progress was never handed down. It was built, argued over, and often paid for by people who never lived to see the result. Last night, you added your chapter to the story, one door knocked, one call made, one neighbor convinced at a time. There's work ahead: lowering costs, improving schools, building housing people can afford, creating government people can trust. We'll get to it, together, and we'll be in touch very soon about how you can support these efforts. But not today. Today, you celebrate. Call a friend. Raise a glass. Dance in the kitchen. Because Democrats, **we f*cking did it.** Sincerely,

**Wednesday, November 4, 2026**
My brother and I were going over the list yesterday.
Turkey. Arroz con gandules. Candied sweet potatoes. Bread stuffing. Salad. Alcapurrias. Flan cheesecake.
"Oh, and I want to make that dip I told you about," he said. "But let's not go overboard. Remember last time? After you left, I kept finding more food. Where it came from, I don't know."
"What are you talking about? We can eat it the next day. It's a little like Sukkot. Thanksgiving is all about having food in abundance."
"What are we having for appetizers?" he asked.
I started thinking back to what we had last year.
There is always room for more.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper. **
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

clean_body: A Thanksgiving table is not meant to be measured. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more A Thanksgiving table is not meant to be measured. | | | Nov 4 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Wednesday, November 4, 2026 My brother and I were going over the list yesterday. Turkey. Arroz con gandules. Candied sweet potatoes. Bread stuffing. Salad. Alcapurrias. Flan cheesecake. "Oh, and I want to make that dip I told you about," he said. "But let's not go overboard. Remember last time? After you left, I kept finding more food. Where it came from, I don't know." "What are you talking about? We can eat it the next day. It's a little like Sukkot. Thanksgiving is all about having food in abundance." "What are we having for appetizers?" he asked. I started thinking back to what we had last year. There is always room for more. Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper. Refuel. Welcome to Sweet Ground. | | ---|---|--- Happy Holidays, America! May your tables hold old traditions, welcome another chair, leave room for new memories --and for a little more than you planned. Thank you.
I'm honored beyond words to be elected as New Hampshire's next U.S. Senator.
Voters said, in a resounding voice, that America needs a course correction. Washington needs a new generation at the table to fix things. And New Hampshire needs independent leadership to stand up and get things done.
Voters in New Hampshire and all across the country have simply had enough and are demanding a change in direction. **And I 'm ready to fight with everything I've got to deliver the change we need.**
New Hampshire, we must be clear-eyed about the scale of the challenges we face and the work it'll take to move forward.
Whether it's building the housing Granite Staters need, expanding access to health care and child care, saving Social Security, protecting our planet, restoring reproductive freedom, rooting out corruption, or holding the administration accountable, we don't have a moment to waste.
There will be moments ahead that test our resolve, and there will be times when we hit roadblocks and get frustrated with the pace of progress.
But we can never give up, and we must be committed to renewing the purpose of American democracy and working with persistence and urgency every day.
I'll be honored to stand shoulder to shoulder with you, to work with anyone willing to deliver for the people of New Hampshire, and to stand up to anyone who tries to set us back.
**Across the state Granite Staters are showing the fighting spirit, resilience, and determination we 're known for.**
That's how we do things in New Hampshire. We step up, we roll up our sleeves, and we make it happen. And that's the spirit I'll bring to my work in the Senate.
_This was a hard-won victory._
Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the corporate special interests threw money, attack ads, and outright lies at us for months. _$67 million worth of it._ But we beat them anyway.
Whether you chipped in, made phone calls, knocked on doors, talked to your friends and neighbors about what's at stake, or simply kept up with our campaign by reading emails like this one. _Thank you._ I wouldn't be here without you.
So as we celebrate, let's think about the brighter future that we will build together. Let's remember what's possible when we join with a common purpose to fight for a freer, fairer New Hampshire.
Let's keep going.
Thank you,
Chris Pappas

body:
The strength of our grassroots movement was on full display last night. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn)
---
Derek, The American people sent a powerful message to Donald Trump and his MAGA cronies in Congress last night. **Democrats across the country swept races up and down the ballot in a historic blue wave. They campaigned on bringing down costs and ending Trump’s rampant corruption. They put in the hard work on the ground, and won. Make no mistake: The strength of our grassroots movement was on _full display_ last night.** We went up against MAGA billionaires hellbent on dismantling our democracy and buying political power for themselves. They thought they could drown out the voice of the people with their chaos, division, and dark money, _but they were wrong_. **Together, we proved them wrong. Together, we proved that, when we stand united, no amount of money can stop the power of the people.** **We all have a lot to be proud of, Derek._Take a moment to feel that pride, that joy, and that relief._** [**But after you take that moment, we need to shift our focus and momentum to our next goal: Keeping control of Congress and taking back the White House in 2028. This fight is far from over, and the work to win in 2028 starts right now. If you're ready to keep building our Democratic movement, please chip in $7 to help us lay the groundwork for electing the next Democratic president and Democrats up and down the ballot in two years.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261104_10234_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn) Our wins this year didn't happen by chance — they were built block by block, neighborhood by neighborhood. Democrats won up and down the ballot across the country, because supporters like you chipped in $5 or $7 at a time to help us. Here’s what their donations funded: Over the past two years, the DNC built a relentless, year-round organizing operation to ensure we’re connecting with voters and communities every single day.
* **Our State Partnership Program** delivered historic funding directly to state Democratic parties, establishing deep, year-round infrastructure nationwide.
* **We built organizing and training programs** that expanded grassroots Democratic power by equipping **_tens of thousands_** of staff, volunteers, and candidates through our national organizing programs. These volunteers made 3.3 million calls and sent 19.2 million texts to get out the vote for our Democratic candidates up and down the ballot in this election.
* **And we focused on Voter Protection & Legal Actions,** taking the Trump administration to court when they tried to undermine voting rights, defending free and fair elections nationwide, and deploying thousands of election observers all across the country to ensure every American could make their voice heard.

**Last night proved that when Democrats invest early, organize tirelessly, and stand up for our values, we win. And, while we’re excited about these victories, we know that our ability to protect our democracy and permanently stop the MAGA agenda in 2028 depends on what we build today.** Instead of resting on our laurels, instead of assuming we have 2028 in the bag, instead of letting victory make us complacent, we’re doubling down on our election-winning programs. And I’m asking you to stay with us in this fight. [**If you can, I hope you’ll consider investing $7 or more in our work to elect Democrats up and down the ballot next election cycle and send a Democrat back to the White House. Your contribution will be put to work immediately.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261104_10234_fr&amount=7&t=7&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.9s4leO&amount=7&refcode=em_20261104_10234_fr&t=8&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn)**

Dear Friend, Yesterday, Rhode Islanders put their trust in me to serve as our next Attorney General. I am incredibly grateful, humbled, and excited for the opportunity to serve the state I love.
---
|
---
First, I want to say thank you. Whether you knocked on doors, made phone calls, donated to our campaign, put up a yard sign, or simply talked to your friends and neighbors about this campaign, you helped make this victory possible. I couldn't have done it without you. Over the past year, I have traveled across Rhode Island and met so many people who care deeply about our state's future. I've heard from parents worried about keeping their kids safe, working families struggling to make ends meet, and Rhode Islanders who want to know that their rights will be protected. Those conversations have shaped this campaign, and they'll guide me every day as Attorney General.
---
|
---
Yesterday was a historic day for our state. For the first time, a majority of Rhode Island's general officers will be women. I'm proud to be a part of this historic moment, and also proud to be the first Democratic woman, the first mom, and the first openly gay person elected Attorney General in our state. I know what these milestones mean, especially to young people who have not always seen themselves represented in positions of leadership. But I also know that what matters most isn't making history. It's what we do with the opportunity we've been given.
---
|
---
I ran for Attorney General because I believe everyone deserves to feel safe in their community, to know their fundamental rights are protected, and to trust that their elected leaders are working every day to make their lives a little easier. That's the work ahead of us. And I promise to bring the same determination, compassion, and commitment to public service that guided this campaign to the Attorney General's Office. My parents taught me that public service is about showing up, listening, and doing the work. That's exactly what I will do as AG. Thank you again for believing in me and for being part of this campaign. Now, let's get to work! Sincerely, Kim

clean_body: | | ~ Dear Friend, Yesterday, Rhode Islanders put their trust in me to serve as our next Attorney General. I am incredibly grateful, humbled, and excited for the opportunity to serve the state I love. | First, I want to say thank you. Whether you knocked on doors, made phone calls, donated to our campaign, put up a yard sign, or simply talked to your friends and neighbors about this campaign, you helped make this victory possible. I couldn't have done it without you. Over the past year, I have traveled across Rhode Island and met so many people who care deeply about our state's future. I've heard from parents worried about keeping their kids safe, working families struggling to make ends meet, and Rhode Islanders who want to know that their rights will be protected. Those conversations have shaped this campaign, and they'll guide me every day as Attorney General. | Yesterday was a historic day for our state. For the first time, a majority of Rhode Island's general officers will be women. I'm proud to be a part of this historic moment, and also proud to be the first Democratic woman, the first mom, and the first openly gay person elected Attorney General in our state. I know what these milestones mean, especially to young people who have not always seen themselves represented in positions of leadership. But I also know that what matters most isn't making history. It's what we do with the opportunity we've been given. | I ran for Attorney General because I believe everyone deserves to feel safe in their community, to know their fundamental rights are protected, and to trust that their elected leaders are working every day to make their lives a little easier. That's the work ahead of us. And I promise to bring the same determination, compassion, and commitment to public service that guided this campaign to the Attorney General's Office. My parents taught me that public service is about showing up, listening, and doing the work. That's exactly what I will do as AG. Thank you again for believing in me and for being part of this campaign. Now, let's get to work! Sincerely, Kim | | ~~ "Instagram" ~~ "Facebook" ~~ "Bluesky" "X" ~~ "YouTube" PAID FOR BY KIM AHERN FOR RHODE ISLAND ~ Want to change how you receive these emails? You can unsubscribe ~~.

Peter, we won!!!

I have wanted to write those words for a long time. After three campaigns, we finally did it. I knew this would take a lot of people coming together, but seeing it happen is something else entirely.

They say the third time's the charm. Maybe so. But I think there is something more to this victory than luck or timing. I think it is what happens when people decide that their voices matter and that the future is worth fighting for.

I hope you know that when I walk into Congress, I will remember the people who inspired me to do this. I will remember the families who are working hard and still struggling to get by. The farmers who carry the weight of uncertainty every season. The small-business owners who have poured everything they have into building something of their own. The young people wondering whether they can afford to build a future here. The seniors who deserve dignity and security. The veterans who have given so much to this country and deserve a government that keeps its promises.

I also want to thank Representative Miller-Meeks for her service to IA-01. We may not have seen eye to eye on many things, but I believe she loves our country, and I appreciate the sacrifice of all those who serve in our government.

I have a lot more to say, and I promise I will. But right now, I mostly just want to say THANK YOU. I am so grateful for your support, so proud of what we accomplished together, and so privileged to go to Congress and represent the place I call home.

— Christina

clean_body: | = Peter, we won!!! I have wanted to write those words for a long time. After three campaigns, we finally did it. subject: Thank You, Texas 21!
body:
This victory belongs to you. I'm grateful for your trust and excited to get to work.

---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter,

Thank you to my family, friends, campaign staff, and the countless supporters who stood with us during this campaign. We could not have won this race without every person who knocked on doors, worked the polls, hosted events, and pitched in to help the cause. I am truly grateful to all of you. And of course, I want to thank all of the voters across the district who placed their trust in me. Nobody will work harder to continue earning that trust.

This victory belongs to the people of Texas’ 21st District. I’m not going to Washington for myself, but rather to be a strong, responsive voice for every family in this district.

Together, we can build a better future for our families, our neighbors, and every community across Texas 21. I’m excited to get to work. I will be praying for all of you and for the future of this great nation.

God bless Texas, and God bless America.

**— Mark “Tex” Teixeira**
21st Congressional District of Texas

body:
I am so grateful for your support.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142887472/658375025/-234467806?refcode=EM_C_261104thanks_N_SB_30DO_5_NG_N_Logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4Y2Q3NjEwMC02NmQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=0Fi5PfZ0NzMVKcJohOadbC709rsltTRqmWI4X29ScG4=) Peter,

It is with great honor and gratitude that I share that **I have been re-elected to represent Ohio’s 11th Congressional District.**

**In my next term, I vow to continue the fight for the future of our nation.** In Congress, we have delivered on big bills, including passing the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which is bringing millions of dollars to repair roads and bridges, capping the price of insulin at $35 a month for seniors, and limiting the cost of prescription drugs to $2,000 a year for seniors. With you by my side, I am ready to get back to work for the American people and preserve our democracy for generations to come.

**With your support, we not only secured my re-election, but Democrats also took back the U.S. House and won big across Ohio!** This includes Amy Acton being elected our next governor and Sherrod Brown flipping Ohio’s Senate seat, and incredible wins in the House – protecting all of our incumbents and flipping major seats for Democrats.

With Trump and his Republican cronies wreaking havoc in Washington, these wins will help restore checks and balances to this out-of-control administration at both the state and federal levels. Finally, our voices will be heard as we fight back against their efforts to dismantle our elections, make healthcare woefully out of reach for millions, slash food security, and more. I vow to take full advantage of this moment to get to work for the people.

**Thank you again for your unwavering support. We could not have done this without you. Now, the real work begins.**

Onward,

Shontel | Shontel Brown is proud to be elected as the Congresswoman for Ohio’s 11th District. She has spent the last decade serving the people of Ohio and building coalitions. As she enters her second full term in Congress, she will use that experience to continue the fight for affordable quality health care, jobs that pay fair wages, a strong public education system, and to preserve and protect our democracy for generations to come. Will you join her and be the change we need?

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

name: Rick Bennett
subject: Thank you
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
Thank you to every single one of you who voted, showed up, and supported this campaign.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Hi Peter, Thank you. Thank you to every single one of you who voted, showed up, and supported this campaign.

I think about the people of this campaign more than you know. On the long days, it was the folks I've met who kept me going; the parent working two jobs and still showing up, the young Mainer wondering if they can afford to build a life in the state they love, the retired couple who told me they'd never given to a campaign before but believed in this one.

Your stories stay with me. Honestly, they're the reason I ran.

You did something most people never do. You didn't wait for someone else to fix things. You stepped up. You gave what you could, at times more than you could, you knocked on doors, you made calls after a long day of work, and you talked to your neighbors about what's possible. That takes courage, and it means more to me than I can put into words.

I promise you this: I will not let you down. I carry what you've told me with me every single day, and I always will.

Maine is worth fighting for. So are you.

With all my heart, thank you.

Rick Bennett
Independent for a Better Maine
---

---

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Austin Davis
body:
And what lies ahead

| |
---
Peter, Last night, voters across Pennsylvania made their voices heard loud and clear, re-electing Governor Josh Shapiro and Lt. Governor Austin Davis, while also sending a Democratic trifecta to Harrisburg for the first time since 1992 to get to work for the folks of the commonwealth. Austin has been at the forefront of these victories raising over $1.5 million to help elect Democrats up and down the ballot. Including: \- $1.2 million for Governor Shapiro’s campaign
\- $102,000 for the PA Coordinated campaign
\- $100,000 to frontline Senate candidates
\- $75,000 to the PA House Democratic Campaign Committee
\- $50,000 to the PA Senate Democratic Campaign Committee He also traveled to every corner of Pennsylvania focused on building the next generation of Democratic leaders, strengthening county and local party organizations, and expanding reach to voters in the commonwealth through digital media. After these historic results, Austin will preside over a Democratic State Senate and continue his nonstop work to fight for the wonderful people of the Keystone State. Austin has set a new standard for what a Lieutenant Governor contributes to a statewide election effort and the results speak for themselves. Thank you for all your hard work to make these victories possible. We couldn’t have done it without you. Now, it’s time to get to work! — Team Davis

clean_body: And what lies ahead | | Peter, Last night, voters across Pennsylvania made their voices heard loud and clear, re-electing Governor Josh Shapiro and Lt. Governor Austin Davis, while also sending a Democratic trifecta to Harrisburg for the first time since 1992 to get to work for the folks of the commonwealth. Austin has been at the forefront of these victories raising over $1.5 million to help elect Democrats up and down the ballot. Including: \- $1.2 million for Governor Shapiro’s campaign \- $102,000 for the PA Coordinated campaign \- $100,000 to frontline Senate candidates \- $75,000 to the PA House Democratic Campaign Committee \- $50,000 to the PA Senate Democratic Campaign Committee He also traveled to every corner of Pennsylvania focused on building the next generation of Democratic leaders, strengthening county and local party organizations, and expanding reach to voters in the commonwealth through digital media. After these historic results, Austin will preside over a Democratic State Senate and continue his nonstop work to fight for the wonderful people of the Keystone State. Austin has set a new standard for what a Lieutenant Governor contributes to a statewide election effort and the results speak for themselves. Thank you for all your hard work to make these victories possible. We couldn’t have done it without you. That's what Charlie lived. That's what Turning Point USA is still fighting for.

name: John Hickenlooper
subject: Thank you
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY HICKENLOOPER FOR COLORADO
body:
Thank you. **I am so proud to be reelected to serve the great state of Colorado in the U.S. Senate.** The message we heard last night is the same one we’ve heard day after day on the road: our fight doesn’t end with Trump. It’s where our fight begins again. Millions of Coloradans made a clear choice: to defend this seat from MAGA's hands and send a real fighter for Colorado back to Washington. My commitment has been and always will be to bring people together and solve problems. Now we’re ready to bring that same focus into this next term. That’s how we’ll tackle this cost-of-living emergency, end this reckless war in Iran, and hold the president accountable for his corruption. But let’s be clear: we have NO interest in just restringing the safety nets Trump chopped down. We want to build a strong floor, finally get universal health coverage, and unrig our economy so the American dream can once again be within reach. There’s a lot of work ahead of us, and we’re so grateful to have you on our side. But it isn’t lost on us that we’ll still face a Trump White House. No doubt they’ll spread lies and try to cheat their way out of losing. No question they’ll try to block and veto our bills. But we’re ready for them. We’re ready to take them on and stop them — just like we did when they tried to sell our public lands and just like we did today. All the hard work that volunteers and campaigns across the country put in is not just about taking back Congress this year. It’s about building the groundwork for kicking Trump and MAGA out of the White House — once and for all — in 2028. We’ll close with this: Thank you, truly. We could not have won this race without you. Thank you to everyone who volunteered, who endorsed this campaign, put up a sign, talked to a friend, chipped in a few bucks, made phone calls, sent texts, or cast a vote. And thank you to the people of Colorado for your continued confidence and trust. I’m honored to represent you in Washington. Now let’s get back to work. With gratitude,
John Hickenlooper

name: True the Vote
subject: 2028 starts today.
body:
We have a country to preserve. And no time to waste.
| | | November 04, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/n4uz4vr7xohvhgw6r99f6h66wrlp7ulhqvn23/x0hph6hem65vdzc5hl/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2Ivdjh1M2hyaDQyZWc5OWFscTIyOXE1c3Z2MGc2bmdhOWgwbHhtMg==) | |
---
|
### 2028 starts today.
Yesterday was a rout. Failed leadership. Squandered opportunities. Too many people entrusted with responsibility who could not find the courage to meet it. But if we come out of this with nothing more than a list of people to blame, we will have wasted even this. Something deeper is happening to our country. And we had better find the courage to face it. We have become careless with an extraordinary inheritance. Careless with our freedom. Careless with the truth. Careless with one another. We enjoy blessings that generations before us sacrificed everything to secure, and somewhere along the way, we began treating those blessings as guarantees. They are not guaranteed. Neither is America. A nation cannot remain free when its people forget what freedom requires. We cannot outsource courage to a candidate, responsibility to a party, or the future of our children to whoever happens to win the next election. We have to become people capable of preserving what we say we love. That requires some brutal honesty. Have we mistaken posting for participating? Have we demanded integrity from public officials while excusing dishonesty when it benefits our side? Have we spent more time condemning strangers than helping our neighbors? Have we become so consumed by what is wrong that we have forgotten to thank God for what is still good—and accept responsibility for protecting it? I am asking myself every one of those questions. There is a spiritual desert beneath all this noise. Ingratitude. Pride. Indifference. Cowardice. The dangerous belief that someone else will do the hard things while we watch. No election can do that soul-searching for us. We need humility enough to examine ourselves and courage enough to change. We need to get on our knees before God, then get on our feet and take responsibility for the work in front of us. To everyone who checked a voter record, helped a friend vote, served at the polls, documented a problem, prayed, volunteered, or gave to keep this work going: thank you. You showed up. Your work mattered. Please hear that today. And hear this, too: we are going to need each other for what comes next. At True the Vote, we will examine our own work with the same scrutiny we ask of others. We will keep pursuing answers, equipping citizens, and insisting on election processes the public can verify. We will keep showing up in the communities where trust has been broken and people have been forgotten. 2028 starts today. Let’s go. Never quit. Isaiah 6:8. Ephesians 6. Game on. Ever onward — |
---
P.S. We have to work harder than we ever have. Starting immediately. And we need your financial support to do it. [_Please make a gift to True the Vote today._](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/n4uz4vr7xohvhgw6r99f6h66wrlp7ulhqvn23/kkhmh6hnpqk023blh7/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl) Help us pursue answers, equip citizens, and stay in the fight for trustworthy elections. Every day between now and 2028 matters.

**Election Night results are not final results.** Mail-in ballots, provisional ballots, and votes from military and overseas Americans can take additional time to count. **Every eligible vote matters, regardless of when it's counted.**

Politicians don't get to declare themselves the winners by throwing out votes they don't like. That's election sabotage, and it threatens to take the power to choose our leaders away from the people.

Congress must monitor federal election counting, investigate interference, and demand enforcement of voting rights protections. And **our representatives must prepare to act wherever credible threats to lawful vote counting emerge**.

**Wednesday, November 4, 2026 -**_****_
_**U.S.:** Democrats win Senate and House in historic landslide, upending President Donald Trump's second term and GOP agenda. Trump is relatively conciliatory in late-night comments. Socialist wins Providence, Rhode Island, mayoral race; city votes to divest from Israel. Major Democratic gubernatorial victories. House flips in Pennsylvania. Other notable House races._
_**Iran:** Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Americans voted "NO TO WAR"; President Donald Trump says he would launch Iran war again despite election losses. Iran claims four oil tankers destroyed by mines in Hormuz, U.S. MQ-9 drone shot down._
_**Palestine:** Palestinian journalist loses 16 kilograms amid solitary confinement in Israeli prison. Israel declares 627 acres of Palestinian land near Ramallah "state property." Israeli forces displace 25 families in Tulkarm, arrest 45 Palestinians across the occupied West Bank. Israel's election committee approves results. Trump says U.S. will cut $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel._

# U.S. News
* **Democrats win Senate and House in historic landslide, upending Trump 's second term and GOP agenda: **Democrats took control of the House of Representatives and the Senate following midterm elections on Tuesday. It is the third time in 50 years that control of both chambers has changed in a single election. Democratic candidates flipped seven seats in the Senate, giving them a 54-46 majority in the upper chamber. The Democrats are estimated to win 258 House seats, and 55 Senate seats. Democrats also won gubernatorial races in Texas, Georgia, Nevada, Ohio, and Iowa.
* **Trump is relatively conciliatory in late-night comments:** President Donald**** Trump congratulated the Democrats in a [call](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b26951-82b8-4bd7-b499-c195339cd2f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to CBS News, saying that he was "looking forward to working with [them] for the good of the country." But on Fox News, he said that he would veto anything passed by Democrats that was "insane," and on Truth Social he posted an image of a hat with "VETO" on it.
* He also [addressed](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b26951-82b8-4bd7-b499-c195339cd2f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the prospect of resuming the Iran war now that the midterms had concluded with CBS, saying the war would conclude "when I say it's over, basically. It'll end when I say it ends."
* **Here are the results from the night 's marquee races:**
* **Democratic victories in "toss-up" Senate races: **Going into the election, seven Senate races were rated "toss-ups" by Cook Political Report: Texas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, Alaska, and Kansas. Democrats won all of those races except for Alaska, which has not yet been called.
* **Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim senator, beating back Islamophobic attacks and pro-Israel opposition:** In Michigan, **Abdul El-Sayed** , a progressive physician, defeated **Mike Rogers** by nearly 10 points to become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. President Trump and other Republicans used Islamophobic rhetoric to rally voters against him. "To AIPAC, who spent $42 million against us, thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you twice," he said in his victory speech.
* **James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa turn Texas blue:** Democrat **James Talarico** defeated Republican **Ken Paxton** in Texas. Talarico, a 37-year-old Democratic state legislator and seminarian, is the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate in Texas since 1993. **Gina Hinojosa** , another state legislator, defeated incumbent governor **Greg Abbott** , making her the first Democrat to win a Texas governor's race since 1995.
* **Annie Andrews ' surprise victory in South Carolina: **The night's biggest upset was in South Carolina, where pediatrician Annie Andrews defeated Darline Graham, the sister of recently deceased Sen. Lindsey Graham and interim Senator appointed to fill his seat in July. Andrews is the first Democrat to represent the state in the Senate since 1998, and is the first woman elected to the post in the state's history.
* **Amy Acton, Sherrod Brown take Ohio:** Democrats **Amy Acton** and **Sherrod Brown** won in Ohio, a state that has been solidly Republican since Trump won the state in 2016. Acton, a former state health official, defeated the Republican **Vivek Ramaswamy** , an entrepreneur and former head of the Department of Government Efficiency. Brown took back a seat he had lost in 2024 to **Bernie Moreno**. Brown previously served for 18 years in the Senate; he is regarded as one of the strongest pro-labor voices in the Democratic Party.
* **Adam Hamilton wins Kansas:** Democrat **Adam Hamilton** , a Methodist pastor, defeated incumbent Republican Sen. **Roger Marshall** , making him the first member of his party to win a Senate seat in Kansas in 94 years. The race attracted huge interest: Political spending topped $110 million, and Trump hosted two rallies in support of the Republican candidate. Hamilton's victory was largely [secured](https://substack.com/redirect/66860c73-68ea-419c-a72a-9cd66f626bd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the state's moderate voters: About seven in 10 moderates backed him over Marshall, according to an AP voter poll. (Read the [Barn Raiser x Drop Site profile of Hamilton](https://substack.com/redirect/d6093a5d-09d5-4581-8c13-f14894666eed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to understand why he won.)
* **Democratic socialists advance in House:** After winning primaries in safe districts, candidates aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America secured victories in the general election. Winners include **Darializa Avila Chevalier** , **Brad Lander** , and **Claire Valdez** in New York City,**Donavan McKinney** in Michigan, **Melat Kiros** in Colorado, **Chris Rabb** in Pennsylvania, and **Analilia Mejia** in New Jersey. **Matt Little** , a progressive running to replace outgoing Rep. **Annie Craig** , won in Minnesota's second congressional district.
* **Mississippi Senate race too close to call:** The Mississippi Senate race remained deadlocked as of Wednesday morning. Democrat **Scott Colom** is in an unexpected dead heat with incumbent GOP Sen. **Cindy Hyde-Smith**. Colom is ahead by just 28 votes out of more than 1 million votes cast. If Colom wins, he would be the state's first Democratic senator since 1982, and its first Black senator since **Blanche K. Bruce** , elected in 1875.
* **Climate activist William Lawrence declares victory in Michigan: William Lawrence** , co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, [declared](https://substack.com/redirect/a00b437e-9ec5-4776-9c1e-48bc57a8d1d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) victory in his Michigan congressional race, citing an unofficial tally that had him up by several percentage points. As of Wednesday morning, he leads his Republican opponent, incumbent **Tom Barrett** , by three percentage points, 51% to 47.8%. Over 95% of votes have been received, according to AP election results.
* **Sanders-backed progressive beats Central Valley, Calif., Republican: Randy Villegas** , a community college professor and son of immigrants, [defeated](https://substack.com/redirect/7137e442-3316-426f-9e92-fe6c809387b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) incumbent Republican Rep. **David Valadao** in California's Central Valley. Villegas received an early endorsement from Sen. **Bernie Sanders** in his primary contest. Valadao, who served five terms in Congress, was one of 10 Republicans who voted to impeach Trump in 2021.
* **Socialist wins Providence, Rhode Island, mayoral race; city votes to divest from Israel:** State representative **David Morales** , a 28-year-old member of the Democratic Socialists of America, was [elected](https://substack.com/redirect/a66f8be2-14c7-4d16-8c75-c4065d2b610a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) mayor of Providence, Rhode Island, easily [defeating](https://substack.com/redirect/c5fa0492-017b-4361-952d-33d162dce488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his Republican opponent, **Dave Talan**. Separately, Providence voters approved a referendum on divesting from "countries and companies committing genocide." The group that organized the referendum, Providence for Palestine, said that the language of the item was a reference to Israel. At least 75 percent of voters supported the measure.
* **Major Democratic gubernatorial victories:** Democrats scored several high-profile gubernatorial victories. In Iowa, State Auditor **Rob Sand** defeated moderate Republican **Zach Lahn** ; in Wisconsin, **David Crowley** defeated Trump-endorsed Rep. **Tom Tiffany** ; and in Michigan, **Jocelyn Benson** defeated Republican Rep. **John James**. Former Atlanta Mayor **Keisha Lance Bottoms** won in Georgia, becoming the first Black female governor in U.S. history. **Deb Haaland** , Secretary of the Interior under **Joe Biden** , won in New Mexico, making her the first Native American to lead a U.S. state.
* **House flips in Pennsylvania:** Democrats flipped two high-profile seats in Pennsylvania. Democrat **Paige Cognetti** , mayor of Scranton, won in Pennsylvania's eighth congressional district, unseating first-term Republican Rep. **Rob Bresnahan**. Democrat **Bob Brooks** , a firefighter, also defeated a first-term Republican incumbent, Rep. **Ryan Mackenzie**.
* **Other notable House races:** Incumbent Republican Rep. **Mario D iaz-Balart** [appeared](https://substack.com/redirect/691be541-2232-47b8-a3a3-6f8b5783e44a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) poised to win in his unexpectedly close re-election race against Democrat **Nicole Locklin**. The Miami-area representative is the longest-serving member of Florida's congressional delegation. **Lauren Boebert** lost in Colorado,**** after switching districts this cycle to one she believed was easier for a Republican to win. **Sam Forstag,** a labor leader backed by **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** , is leading the Republican in Montana's first congressional district, but the race has not been called. **Richard Ojeda,** a former state senator in West Virginia known for supporting the 2018 teachers' strike, won in North Carolina.

📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com
# Iran
* **Iran 's Ghalibaf says Americans voted "NO TO WAR"; Trump says he would launch Iran war again despite election losses:** American voters rejected the war with Iran in the midterm elections, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Wednesday, [writing](https://substack.com/redirect/de9f77c4-6651-423a-a02c-6d9166f97de6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, "Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message."
* He added that if the U.S. government "betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare."
* President Trump said on Tuesday that the war with Iran contributed to Republican losses. "Part of it was Iran," Trump told Fox News. In a separate interview with the Wall Street Journal, Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3c337aa1-8323-4d0f-b433-22e290fd3072?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he did not regret launching the war: "I did the right thing. I would have done it again."
* **Trump says U.S. "locked and loaded" for Iran strikes but has no immediate plans to attack:** Trump [downplayed](https://substack.com/redirect/016bc8d7-0367-4734-ab08-fb89304c830d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) speculation of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran following the midterm elections, telling the Financial Times that Washington had no immediate plans to attack despite indications from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that strikes could take place later this week. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," Trump said.
* Referring to ongoing negotiations with Tehran, he added, "We seem to be getting everything we want." Trump said the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports was damaging Tehran's economy, calling it "a brilliant situation."
* Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said that Tehran remained committed to diplomatic talks through its seven-day roadmap presented to Qatari mediators but was "ready for any scenario." Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned that any renewed U.S. attacks would result in "much broader dimensions" of war.
* **Europe approaches winter with lowest gas reserves since 2013 amid Hormuz supply disruptions:** Europe is approaching the winter season with its lowest natural gas storage levels in more than a decade, raising the risk of tight global gas supplies and higher prices through 2027, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/cde2f00f-4eb7-4af7-a0ed-68c7be0079e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the International Energy Agency. The effective halt of liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has cut exports from Qatar and the UAE by more than 60 billion cubic meters between March and October, pushing Asian and European gas prices to their highest levels since the 2022-23 energy crisis.
* **Iran claims four oil tankers destroyed by mines in Hormuz, U.S. MQ-9 drone shot down:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/98436a91-34d7-47da-a894-c709e9db1855?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that four oil tankers attempting to cross a "prohibited" corridor south of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines and were destroyed, with the vessels still burning. Two other vessels were stopped, according to the IRGC.
* The group also claimed its air defense forces shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone over the strait, bringing the number of MQ-9 drones it says it has downed to 56.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed three Palestinians--two in new attacks and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and injured 21 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,618 killed and 175,920 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,602 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,794, while 847 bodies have been recovered.
* **Palestinian journalist loses 16 kilograms amid solitary confinement in Israeli prison:** Palestinian journalist Bushra Al-Tawil, from Al-Bireh in the occupied West Bank, lost 16 kilograms since her arrest on February 5, amid severe food shortages, medical neglect, and prolonged solitary confinement, according to the Palestinian Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs.
* Al-Tawil has been held in isolation since August 17 and is currently detained at Israel's Ohalei Oz prison. Her isolation was extended for another month on November 2.
* The commission said that she is suffering from dark skin lesions caused by scabies, as well as painful tendon inflammation in her hands and feet. Israeli prison authorities have ignored repeated requests for medical treatment.
* **Israel declares 627 acres of Palestinian land near Ramallah "state property":** Israeli authorities [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/be9c735a-d38b-4d9a-a087-9679c7333537?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an order on November 3 declaring 627 acres (2,536 dunams) of Palestinian land in Beitillu, Al-Mazra'a Al-Qibliya, and Deir Ammar, northwest of Ramallah in the West Bank, as "state property," according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission.
* The land surrounds the Israeli settlement of Kerem Reim, and the commission warned that the declaration would facilitate the expansion of settlements. Palestinian landowners have 45 days from the order's publication to file legal objections.
* **Israeli forces displace 25 families in Tulkarm, arrest 45 Palestinians across the West Bank:** Israeli forces carried out raids, demolitions, and arrests across the West Bank on Wednesday, WAFA reported. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society reported at least 45 arrests, including five women and two journalists.
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [forcibly displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/d78cfa05-0184-4e29-babd-977de4d9ef67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 25 families from homes near Tulkarm refugee camp, converting some into military barracks. Israel's assault on the Tulkarm, Nur Shams, and Jenin refugee camps has continued for 647 days, displacing more than 32,000 Palestinians in what Human Rights Watch found amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity.
* **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/6ae455d2-18fa-46f1-b2f9-0b2f642a9f54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tear gas toward a school in Al-Mughayyer, causing students to suffer from tear gas inhalation. Soldiers also detained a teacher and closed the school entrance.
* **Tubas/Northern Jordan Valley:** Israeli bulldozers [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/3f230040-df5e-4953-8c35-ea8471d9bfbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) residential and livestock structures belonging to three Palestinians in the Al-Deir area of the northern Jordan Valley.
* **Hebron:** Under military protection, armed Israeli settlers [destroyed](https://substack.com/redirect/64f19a06-ae35-40d0-a5fe-c5807a64fdb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive trees in Surif, northwest of Hebron.
* **Israel 's election committee approves results:** Israel's Central Elections Committee presidium [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/24df4233-480b-476d-ac01-40d6273acbee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday to certify last week's election results, despite efforts by Netanyahu's Likud party and other outgoing coalition parties to delay certification over unsubstantiated claims of election fraud.
* The committee found no irregularities indicating that the vote had been compromised, it said. The results will be submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, after which he will consult party leaders on whom to task with forming the next government.
* **Trump says U.S. will cut $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel:** The U.S. will stop providing $4 billion in aid each year to Israel "at the end of the year," President Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3d2eb96c-d4be-4a1a-bcb6-454d31994e23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday, but will sell arms to Tel Aviv. "We give them $4 billion of things and money, and they don't need it. And I was approached by Bibi Netanyahu, and we've been talking about it for a couple of years because it's a lot of money," Trump told Fox News as voting was underway. "Why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don't need it?" he said, a reference to Abdul El-Sayed, a forthright critic of Israel who was elected in Michigan to the U.S. Senate.
* Trump's announcement comes as Congress considers phasing out aid to Israel, instead expanding U.S.-Israel cooperation in the countries' military-industrial operations.
* In 2016, President Barack Obama signed an unprecedented security agreement giving Israel $38 billion to its military over 10 years, which is set to expire in 2028. Trump seemed to suggest on Tuesday that he may cancel the agreement two years early, with Israel's consent, though such a decision would probably require Congressional approval. Even if U.S. aid were suddenly cut, there are still many years of already purchased weaponry yet to be delivered, according to AP.

# Yemen
* **20+ killed in Ansarallah missile strike on Saudi-backed government camp:** More than 20 people were killed, and several others wounded, in an Ansarallah ballistic missile [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/369f4146-69f6-4e8d-97b8-5f463789aef3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) targeting a military training camp in the Maris area of Dhale governorate, Sky News Arabia reported.
* Meanwhile, Saudi-backed forces claimed that they captured the Al-Dahida heights and surrounding areas in eastern Al-Jawf governorate, backed by airstrikes targeting Ansarallah positions and supply lines.
* The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia announced that a second Indian national injured in the October 10 Ansarallah attack on Riyadh airport had died, following an attack that killed at least 12 people and wounded hundreds.
* **Hezbollah denies sending military experts to Yemen:** Lebanon's Hezbollah denied claims that its military experts are operating in Yemen and helping Ansarallah develop weapons, train fighters, and manage military operations.
* On Tuesday, the Yemeni Saudi-backed government claimed that 21 foreign military experts, including 14 from Iran's IRGC and seven from Hezbollah, were working with Ansarallah. Their roles extended beyond financing, arming, and training fighters to directly overseeing military operations and political and media activities, according to the government.
* In a statement on Wednesday, Hezbollah called the accusations "completely baseless." The group said that Yemenis can defend their country without outside intervention, and called for dialogue to preserve Yemen's unity and sovereignty.

# Lebanon
* **Again violating ceasefire, Israeli forces burn homes and shell towns in southern Lebanon:** Israeli forces [set fire](https://substack.com/redirect/1cbcb2cd-8530-4933-b9cf-538d1e3de6c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to homes in the town of Hadatha in the Bint Jbeil district, while Israeli artillery shelled Baraachit in the same district, violating the ceasefire, Lebanon's National News Agency reported on Wednesday. Israeli forces also [shelled](https://substack.com/redirect/7b7c1b99-4361-4a11-9abf-13096c009869?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Mansouri and Wadi Zibqin in the Tyre (Sour) district earlier in the morning.
